name: Alchemist
flavor_text: An Alchemist is an expert at combining reagents to produce mystical effects. They use their mastery of alchemy to create potions, elixirs, and other concoctions that can heal, harm, and alter.
description: The Alchemist is the support specialist of the Artificer class, focusing on creating experimental elixirs and amplifying the healing and damage of their spells. They are masters of magical chemistry, able to produce a variety of beneficial potions and enhance their acid, fire, and poison-based magic.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Tool Proficiency (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with alchemist's supplies. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan's tools of your choice.

features.name: Alchemist Spells (3rd Level)
features.description: You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown on the Alchemist Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

features.name: Experimental Elixir (3rd Level)
features.description: Whenever you finish a long rest, you can magically produce an experimental elixir in an empty flask you touch. Roll on the Experimental Elixir table for the elixir's effect. You can create additional elixirs by expending a spell slot of 1st level or higher for each one. At 6th level you can make two elixirs at the end of a long rest, and three at 15th level.

features.name: Alchemical Savant (5th Level)
features.description: Whenever you cast a spell using your alchemist's supplies as the spellcasting focus, you gain a bonus to one roll of the spell. That roll must restore hit points or be a damage roll that deals acid, fire, necrotic, or poison damage, and the bonus equals your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

features.name: Restorative Reagents (9th Level)
features.description: Whenever a creature drinks an experimental elixir you created, it gains temporary hit points equal to 2d6 + your Intelligence modifier. You can also cast Lesser Restoration without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier per long rest.

features.name: Chemical Mastery (15th Level)
features.description: You gain resistance to acid damage and are immune to the poisoned condition. You can also cast Greater Restoration and Heal once each per long rest without expending a spell slot.

name: Armorer
flavor_text: An artificer who specializes as an Armorer modifies armor to function almost like a second skin. The armor is enhanced to hone the artificer's magic, unleash potent attacks, and generate a formidable defense. The artificer bonds with this armor, becoming one with it even as they experiment with it and refine its magical capabilities.
description: The Armorer is a front-line tank who turns their armor into a weapon and a spellcasting focus. They can customize their Arcane Armor into one of two models—Guardian (for defense and thunder damage) or Infiltrator (for stealth and lightning damage)—allowing them to adapt to different combat roles.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Tool Proficiencies (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.

features.name: Arcane Armor (3rd Level)
features.description: As an action, you can turn a suit of armor you are wearing into Arcane Armor, provided you have smith's tools in hand. You gain several benefits: the armor lacks a Strength requirement for you, it can be used as a spellcasting focus, it attaches to you and can't be removed against your will, and it replaces any missing limbs.

features.name: Armor Model (3rd Level)
features.description: You can customize your Arcane Armor, choosing between Guardian and Infiltrator. Each model grants a special weapon that can use your Intelligence modifier for attack and damage rolls. You can change the model on a short or long rest.

features.name: Guardian
features.description: Gains Thunder Gauntlets (1d8 thunder damage, imposes disadvantage on attacks against others) and a Defensive Field (bonus action for temporary HP).

features.name: Infiltrator
features.description: Gains a Lightning Launcher (ranged, 1d6 lightning damage), Powered Steps (+5 ft. speed), and a Dampening Field (advantage on Stealth checks).

features.name: Extra Attack (5th Level)
features.description: You can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Armor Modifications (9th Level)
features.description: Your Arcane Armor becomes more potent, gaining additional benefits based on your chosen model (e.g., Guardian's Thunder Gauntlets deal more damage, Infiltrator's Lightning Launcher gains extra range).

features.name: Perfected Armor (15th Level)
features.description: Your Armor Model gains a final, powerful enhancement (e.g., Guardian can pull enemies toward it, Infiltrator can become invisible).

name: Artillerist
flavor_text: An Artillerist specializes in using magic to hurl energy, projectiles, and explosions on a battlefield. Along with their massive destructive power, Artillerists must also be proficient in the creation of emplacements and fortifications.
description: The Artillerist is the damage-dealing blaster of the Artificer subclasses. They create an Eldritch Cannon—a magical, customizable turret—that can be configured to fire different types of projectiles, and they learn spells that incinerate and control the battlefield.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Tool Proficiency (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with woodcarver's tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan's tools of your choice.

features.name: Artillerist Spells (3rd Level)
features.description: You always have certain spells prepared (e.g., Shield, Thunderwave, Scorching Ray, Shatter) that count as artificer spells for you but don’t count against your prepared spells.

features.name: Eldritch Cannon (3rd Level)
features.description: Using smith's tools, you can take a bonus action to magically create an Eldritch Cannon in an unoccupied space on a horizontal surface within 5 feet of you. The cannon is a magical object with AC 15 and hit points equal to three times your Artificer level. You choose its type when you create it:

features.name: Flamethrower
features.description: Emits a 15-foot cone of fire (Dexterity save for half damage).

features.name: Force Ballista
features.description: Makes a ranged spell attack for force damage and can push the target.

features.name: Protector
features.description: Emits a burst of positive energy that grants temporary hit points to allies in a 10-foot radius.

features.name: Arcane Firearm (5th Level)
features.description: You can use your woodcarver's tools to carve runes into a wand, staff, or rod, turning it into an Arcane Firearm. When you cast an artificer spell through it, you add 1d8 to one damage roll of the spell.

features.name: Explosive Cannon (9th Level)
features.description: Your Eldritch Cannon becomes more powerful. Its damage increases, and you can detonate it as a reaction when it is destroyed or when you dismiss it, creating an explosion that damages nearby creatures.

features.name: Fortified Position (15th Level)
features.description: You can create two Eldritch Cannons with a single bonus action (using separate spell slots), and you and your allies gain half cover while within 10 feet of a cannon.

name: Battle Smith
flavor_text: A Battle Smith is a combination of protector and medic, an expert at defending others and repairing both materiel and personnel. To aid in their work, Battle Smiths are accompanied by a Steel Defender, a protective companion of their own creation.
description: The Battle Smith is a gish-style Artificer who excels in direct combat. They gain proficiency with martial weapons and can use their Intelligence modifier for weapon attacks. They are accompanied by a Steel Defender—a loyal construct companion—and can channel magical energy to either damage foes or heal allies.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Tool Proficiency (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with smith's tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan's tools of your choice. You also craft ordinary or magic weapons in half the time.

features.name: Battle Smith Spells (3rd Level)
features.description: You always have certain spells prepared (e.g., Heroism, Shield, Warding Bond, Aura of Life) that count as artificer spells for you.

features.name: Battle Ready (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons. When you attack with a magic weapon, you can use your Intelligence modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, for the attack and damage rolls.

features.name: Steel Defender (3rd Level)
features.description: Your tinkering has borne you a companion, a Steel Defender. It is friendly to you and your allies, obeys your commands, and acts during your turn (you can command it with a bonus action). If it has died within the last hour, you can revive it by expending a spell slot.

features.name: Extra Attack (5th Level)
features.description: You can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Arcane Jolt (9th Level)
features.description: When you or your Steel Defender hits a target, you can channel magical energy to either deal an extra 2d6 force damage or restore 2d6 hit points to a creature or object within 30 feet. You can use this a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier per long rest.

features.name: Improved Defender (15th Level)
features.description: Your Arcane Jolt damage and healing increase to 4d6. Your Steel Defender gains a +2 bonus to AC, and when it uses its Deflect Attack reaction, the attacker takes force damage equal to 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier.

name: Cartographer
flavor_text: Cartographers are Artificers who master the craft of maps and magical ink to lead allies through danger. These premier navigators are crucial for any treacherous expedition, whether upon an elemental airship, nautical vessel, or part of an overground caravan.
description: The Cartographer is a support-oriented Artificer who uses magical maps to coordinate the party, enhance movement, and provide strategic advantages. They excel at exploration, teleportation, and keeping the party connected across the battlefield.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Tools of the Trade (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with Calligrapher’s Supplies and Cartographer’s Tools. You also scribe Spell Scrolls in half the time.

features.name: Cartographer Spells (3rd Level)
features.description: You always have certain spells prepared, including Faerie Fire, Guiding Bolt, Healing Word, Clairvoyance, Locate Object, and Teleportation Circle. Adventurer’s Atlas (3rd Level): After each long rest, you can create a number of magical maps (equal to 1 + your Intelligence modifier) and distribute them to creatures. A creature holding a map adds 1d4 to its initiative rolls and always knows the location of other map holders on the same plane. Map holders can also target each other with spells and effects that require sight, ignoring cover and obscurement, as long as the target is in range.

features.name: Mapping Magic (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain two benefits: Illuminated Cartography (cast Faerie Fire without a spell slot a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier per long rest) and Portal Jump (spend half your speed to teleport up to 10 feet, or to a space within 5 feet of a map holder within 30 feet).

features.name: Guided Precision (5th Level)
features.description: Once per turn, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of a Cartographer spell or to an attack that hits a creature affected by your Faerie Fire. Additionally, taking damage can’t break your concentration on Faerie Fire.

features.name: Ingenious Movement (9th Level)
features.description: Whenever you use your Flash of Genius feature, you or a willing creature you can see within 30 feet can teleport up to 30 feet as part of that same reaction.

features.name: Superior Atlas (15th Level)
features.description: Your Adventurer’s Atlas improves with three benefits:

features.name: Safe Haven
features.description: When a map holder drops to 0 HP but isn’t killed outright, they can destroy their map to teleport next to you or another map holder and become stable.

features.name: Unerring Path
features.description: While holding a map, you can cast Find the Path once per long rest without a spell slot.

features.name: Unshakeable Mind
features.description: While at least one of your maps exists, taking damage can’t break your concentration on Artificer spells.

name: Path of the Berserker
flavor_text: For some barbarians, rage is a means to an end—that end being violence. The Path of the Berserker is a path of untrammeled fury, slick with blood.
description: The archetypal barbarian. You sacrifice defense for overwhelming offense, entering a Frenzy that grants a bonus-action attack each turn, shrugging off mind-altering effects, and terrifying your foes with your presence.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Frenzy (3rd Level)
features.description: When you rage, you can go into a frenzy. For the duration, you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion.

features.name: Mindless Rage (6th Level)
features.description: You can’t be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration.

features.name: Intimidating Presence (10th Level)
features.description: As an action, you can frighten one creature within 30 feet with your menacing presence. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature again after a short or long rest.

features.name: Retaliation (14th Level)
features.description: When you take damage from a creature within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

name: Path of the Ancestral Guardian
flavor_text: Barbarians who draw on their ancestral guardians can better fight to protect their tribes and their allies. To cement ties to these spirits, they cover themselves in elaborate tattoos that celebrate their ancestors’ deeds.
description: A protective tank. You summon spectral warriors that hinder enemies who attack your allies, and you can project a Spirit Shield to reduce damage dealt to your companions.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Ancestral Protectors (3rd Level)
features.description: While raging, when you hit a creature with an attack, spectral warriors appear, and the target becomes marked. While marked, it has disadvantage on attack rolls against anyone other than you, and if it hits another creature, that creature has resistance to the damage dealt.

features.name: Spirit Shield (6th Level)
features.description: While raging, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage dealt to another creature within 30 feet by 2d6. This reduction increases to 3d6 at 10th level and 4d6 at 14th level.

features.name: Consult the Spirits (10th Level)
features.description: You can cast Augury or Clairvoyance without expending a spell slot or material components, but only as rituals.

features.name: Vengeful Ancestors (14th Level)
features.description: When you use Spirit Shield, the attacker takes force damage equal to the damage you prevented.

name: Path of the Battlerager
flavor_text: Known as Kuldjargh (literally “axe idiot”) in Dwarvish, battleragers are dwarf followers of the gods of war. They specialize in wearing bulky, spiked armor and throwing themselves into combat, striking with their body itself.
description: A grappling-focused dwarf who turns their spiked armor into a weapon. You can attack with your armor spikes, damage creatures that grapple you or that you grapple, and eventually charge across the battlefield while raging.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Battlerager Armor (3rd Level)
features.description: While wearing spiked armor and raging, you can use a bonus action to make a melee weapon attack with your armor spikes (1d6 piercing, using Strength). Creatures that grapple you or that you grapple take piercing damage.

features.name: Reckless Abandon (6th Level)
features.description: When you use Reckless Attack while raging, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).

features.name: Battlerager Charge (10th Level)
features.description: While raging, you can take the Dash action as a bonus action.

features.name: Spiked Retribution (14th Level)
features.description: When a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack while you are raging and wearing spiked armor, it takes 3 piercing damage.

name: Path of the Beast
flavor_text: Barbarians who walk the Path of the Beast draw their rage from a bestial spark burning within their souls. That beast bursts forth in the throes of rage, physically transforming the barbarian.
description: A shapeshifting barbarian. When you rage, you manifest natural weapons—Bite, Claws, or Tail—each with unique benefits. You eventually gain magical natural weapons, adapt to your environment, and curse foes with rabid fury.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Form of the Beast (3rd Level)
features.description: When you rage, choose a natural weapon:

features.name: Bite
features.description: Deals 1d8 piercing damage; once per turn when you damage a creature with it, you can regain hit points equal to your proficiency bonus if you are below half your hit point maximum.

features.name: Claws
features.description: Each hand becomes a claw dealing 1d6 slashing damage; once per turn when you attack with a claw using the Attack action, you can make one additional claw attack.

features.name: Tail
features.description: Deals 1d8 piercing damage and has the reach property; you can use your reaction to add a d8 to your AC against one attack.

features.name: Bestial Soul (6th Level)
features.description: Your natural weapons count as magical. After a rest, choose one adaptation: a swimming speed and water breathing, a climbing speed, or the ability to extend your jump with a Strength (Athletics) check.

features.name: Infectious Fury (10th Level)
features.description: When you hit a creature with your natural weapon while raging, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it either uses its reaction to attack another creature of your choice or takes 2d12 psychic damage.

features.name: Call the Hunt (14th Level)
features.description: When you rage, you can grant a number of allies temporary hit points and the ability to deal extra damage.

name: Path of the Giant
flavor_text: Giants are paragons of primordial power, once intended by Annam the All-Father to rule over all the Material Plane. As a Path of the Giant barbarian, you tap into these same primal forces to surge with elemental energy and tower over your foes.
description: A size-and-elemental focused barbarian. Your rage makes you Large, extends your reach, and empowers thrown weapons. You can infuse weapons with elemental energy, hurl enemies across the battlefield, and eventually become a Huge force of nature.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: General Feature
features.description: Giant’s Power (3rd Level): You learn the Druidcraft or Thaumaturgy cantrip and can speak, read, and write Giant.

features.name: General Feature
features.description: Giant’s Havoc (3rd Level): While raging, you become Large, your reach increases by 5 feet, and you can add your Rage Damage bonus to damage rolls with thrown weapons.

features.name: Elemental Cleaver (6th Level)
features.description: You can infuse a weapon with elemental energy, changing its damage type and granting it the thrown property. The weapon magically returns to your hand after each attack.

features.name: Mighty Impel (10th Level)
features.description: You can throw a smaller creature or object instead of making an attack, forcing it to make a saving throw to avoid being hurled.

features.name: Demiurgic Colossus (14th Level)
features.description: Your size increases to Huge while raging, and your reach and thrown damage increase further.

name: Path of the Storm Herald
flavor_text: Barbarians who follow the Path of the Storm Herald learn to transform their rage into a mantle of primal magic that swirls around them. When in a fury, they tap into nature to create powerful, magical effects.
description: An aura-based barbarian. You choose an environment—Desert, Sea, or Tundra—that determines the effect of your Storm Aura while raging. You eventually gain resistances, protect allies with your storm, and intensify the aura’s power.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Storm Aura (3rd Level)
features.description: While raging, you emanate a 10-foot aura. Choose Desert (fire damage to creatures in the aura), Sea (lightning damage to one creature), or Tundra (cold damage and reduced speed). The damage increases at higher levels.

features.name: Storm Soul (6th Level)
features.description: You gain a benefit based on your chosen environment: Desert (fire resistance), Sea (lightning resistance), or Tundra (cold resistance). You also gain a minor utility ability (e.g., setting fires, breathing underwater, or freezing water).

features.name: Shielding Storm (10th Level)
features.description: You and allies within your aura gain resistance to the damage type of your Storm Aura.

features.name: Raging Storm (14th Level)
features.description: Your aura grows to 15 feet, and creatures affected by it have their speed halved. The damage of your aura increases.

name: Path of the Totem Warrior
flavor_text: The Path of the Totem Warrior is a spiritual journey, as the barbarian accepts a spirit animal as guide, protector, and inspiration. In battle, your totem spirit fills you with supernatural might, adding magical fuel to your rage.
description: A versatile, spirit-guided barbarian. You choose a totem animal (Bear, Eagle, Elk, Tiger, or Wolf) at 3rd, 6th, and 14th level, gaining different benefits each time, allowing you to customize your playstyle.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Spirit Seeker (3rd Level)
features.description: You can cast Beast Sense and Speak with Animals as rituals.

features.name: Totem Spirit (3rd Level)
features.description: Choose a totem:

features.name: Bear
features.description: While raging, you have resistance to all damage except psychic damage.

features.name: Eagle
features.description: While raging and not wearing heavy armor, opportunity attacks against you have disadvantage, and you can Dash as a bonus action.

features.name: Wolf
features.description: While raging, allies have advantage on melee attack rolls against creatures within 5 feet of you.

features.name: Aspect of the Beast (6th Level)
features.description: Gain a magical benefit based on your totem (e.g., Bear: double carrying capacity; Eagle: see up to a mile away; Wolf: track at a fast pace).

features.name: Totemic Attunement (14th Level)
features.description: Gain a powerful ability based on your totem (e.g., Bear: while raging, creatures within 5 feet are hostile to you have disadvantage on attacks against targets other than you).

name: Path of Wild Magic
flavor_text: Many places in the multiverse abound with beauty, intense emotion, and rampant magic. Barbarians are especially susceptible to these wild influences, with some being transformed by the magic. These magic-suffused barbarians walk the Path of Wild Magic.
description: A chaotic barbarian whose rage triggers random magical effects. You can sense magic, unleash a Wild Surge when you rage (rolling on a table of beneficial effects), and eventually bolster allies with your magic or control the chaos.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Magic Awareness (3rd Level)
features.description: As an action, you can cast Detect Magic without a spell slot, using Strength as your spellcasting ability. You can use this a number of times equal to your Strength modifier per long rest.

features.name: Wild Surge (3rd Level)
features.description: When you enter your rage, roll on the Wild Magic table to determine a magical effect (e.g., teleporting, damaging nearby foes, gaining temporary hit points, or infusing a weapon with force damage).

features.name: Bolstering Magic (6th Level)
features.description: As an action, you can touch a creature (including yourself) and grant it a bonus d3 to ability checks and attack rolls, or restore a spell slot. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

features.name: Unstable Backlash (10th Level)
features.description: When you take damage or fail a saving throw while raging, you can use your reaction to roll on the Wild Magic table and immediately produce a new effect.

features.name: Controlled Surge (14th Level)
features.description: When you roll on the Wild Magic table, you can roll twice and choose either result.

name: Path of the Zealot
flavor_text: Barbarians who walk the Path of the Zealot receive boons from a god or pantheon. These barbarians experience their rage as an ecstatic episode of divine union that infuses them with power.
description: A divinely empowered barbarian. You deal extra radiant or necrotic damage, can be revived without material components, reroll failed saves, and inspire allies with a divine battle cry.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Divine Fury (3rd Level)
features.description: While raging, the first creature you hit on each of your turns with a weapon or unarmed strike takes extra damage equal to 1d6 + half your barbarian level (rounded down). The damage is necrotic or radiant (your choice).

features.name: Warrior of the Gods (3rd Level)
features.description: You have a pool of four d12s that you can spend as a bonus action to heal yourself. The pool grows to five dice at 6th level, six at 12th, and seven at 17th.

features.name: Fanatical Focus (6th Level)
features.description: Once per rage, if you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and you must use the new roll.

features.name: Zealous Presence (10th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you unleash a battle cry. Up to ten creatures of your choice within 60 feet gain advantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Rage Beyond Death (14th Level)
features.description: While raging, you can’t be killed by dropping to 0 hit points; you still make death saving throws, but you don’t fall unconscious until your rage ends.

name: Path of the Brute
flavor_text: Barbarians are by their nature brutish and savage in their ways, using their great Strength and heavy-built Constitution to destroy their foes and shrug off the greatest of hits. Some barbarians are quite literally Brutes by their nature—forceful and mean-spirited, knowing only power and force.
description: A homebrew subclass focused on raw, unthinking aggression. You sacrifice mental faculties for greater accuracy and damage, always have advantage on Reckless Attacks, and can even shrug off being stunned or paralyzed.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material (this is homebrew content from D&D Wiki).

features.name: Brute Force (3rd Level)
features.description: Any attack that benefits from your Rage bonus damage gains an additional +2 to attack and damage rolls. However, you have disadvantage on all Intelligence and Wisdom checks and saving throws while raging.

features.name: Savagery (6th Level)
features.description: No matter the circumstances, your Reckless Attacks are always made at advantage.

features.name: Hard Headed (10th Level)
features.description: If you are stunned or paralyzed, you can enter a rage to suspend the effect for the duration of the rage.

features.name: Brute Force Savagery (14th Level)
features.description: Further improvements to your brutal strikes (specific features depend on the homebrew revision).

name: College of Creation
flavor_text: Bards believe the cosmos is a work of art—the creation of the first dragons and gods. That creative work included harmonies that continue to resound through existence today, a power known as the Song of Creation. The bards of the College of Creation draw on that primeval song through dance, music, and poetry, and their teachers share this lesson: "Before the sun and the moon, there was the Song, and its music awoke the first dawn. Its melodies so delighted the stones and trees that some of them gained a voice of their own. And now they sing too. Learn the Song, students, and you too can teach the mountains to sing and dance."
description: A bard who channels the primordial Song of Creation to conjure objects from nothing, animate inanimate items, and empower their Bardic Inspiration with reality-shaping effects.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Mote of Potential (3rd Level)
features.description: When you give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die, you can create a Tiny mote of potential that orbits it. When the die is used, the mote provides an additional effect: for an ability check, the creature rolls the die again and chooses; for an attack roll, the target and nearby creatures take thunder damage equal to the roll; for a saving throw, the creature gains temporary hit points equal to the roll + your Charisma modifier.

features.name: Performance of Creation (3rd Level)
features.description: As an action, you create one nonmagical item of your choice in an unoccupied space within 10 feet. The item's gp value can't exceed 20 times your bard level, and it must be Medium or smaller. It lasts for hours equal to your proficiency bonus. You can use this feature again by expending a spell slot of 2nd level or higher. The maximum size increases to Large at 6th level and Huge at 14th level.

features.name: Animating Performance (6th Level)
features.description: As an action, you animate one Large or smaller nonmagical item within 30 feet. It uses the Dancing Item stat block, is friendly to you and your allies, and obeys your commands. It lasts for 1 hour or until reduced to 0 hit points. You can command it as part of the same bonus action you use for Bardic Inspiration. You can use this feature again by expending a spell slot of 3rd level or higher.

features.name: Creative Crescendo (14th Level)
features.description: When you use Performance of Creation, you can create a number of items equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of two) instead of one. Only one item can be of the maximum size you can create; the rest must be Small or Tiny. You are no longer limited by gp value when creating items with Performance of Creation.

name: College of Eloquence
flavor_text: Adherents of the College of Eloquence master the art of oratory. Persuasion is regarded as a high art, and a well-reasoned, well-spoken argument often proves more powerful than objective truth. These bards wield a blend of logic and theatrical wordplay, winning over skeptics and detractors with logical arguments, and plucking at heartstrings to appeal to the emotions of entire audiences.
description: A silver-tongued orator who can never roll poorly on social checks, weakens enemies' saving throws with unsettling words, ensures their inspiration is never wasted, and can inspire others even when their own inspiration succeeds.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Silver Tongue (3rd Level)
features.description: When you make a Charisma (Persuasion) or Charisma (Deception) check, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

features.name: Unsettling Words (3rd Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and choose one creature within 60 feet. Roll the die; the creature must subtract the number rolled from the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

features.name: Unfailing Inspiration (6th Level)
features.description: When a creature adds one of your Bardic Inspiration dice to an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw and the roll fails, the creature can keep the Bardic Inspiration die.

features.name: Universal Speech (6th Level)
features.description: As an action, choose up to your Charisma modifier creatures within 60 feet. They can magically understand you, regardless of the language you speak, for 1 hour. You can use this feature again by expending a spell slot.

features.name: Infectious Inspiration (14th Level)
features.description: When a creature within 60 feet adds one of your Bardic Inspiration dice to a roll and succeeds, you can use your reaction to give a different creature within 60 feet a Bardic Inspiration die without expending a use. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier per long rest.

name: College of Glamour
flavor_text: The College of Glamour traces its origins to the beguiling magic of the Feywild. Bards who study this magic weave threads of beauty and terror into their songs and stories, and the mightiest among them can cloak themselves in otherworldly majesty. Their performances stir up wistful longing for forgotten innocence, evoke unconscious memories of long-held fears, and tug at the emotions of even the most hard-hearted listeners.
description: A fey-touched bard who inspires allies with supernatural vigor, charms or frightens foes with their performances, and eventually assumes an unearthly majesty that makes them impossible to attack.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Beguiling Magic (3rd Level)
features.description: You always have Charm Person and Mirror Image prepared. Immediately after you cast an Enchantment or Illusion spell using a spell slot, you can force one creature within 60 feet to make a Wisdom save or be charmed or frightened (your choice) for 1 minute. You can restore this use by expending a Bardic Inspiration use.

features.name: Mantle of Inspiration (3rd Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can expend a Bardic Inspiration die. Choose a number of creatures within 60 feet equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). Each gains temporary hit points equal to twice the number rolled and can use its reaction to move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

features.name: Mantle of Majesty (6th Level)
features.description: You always have Command prepared. As a bonus action, you cast Command without expending a spell slot and take on an unearthly appearance for 1 minute (concentration). During this time, you can cast Command as a bonus action without a slot, and creatures charmed by you automatically fail their saves against it. You can restore this use by expending a 3rd-level or higher spell slot.

features.name: Unbreakable Majesty (14th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you assume a majestic presence for 1 minute. Any creature that attacks you for the first time on a turn must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or the attack automatically misses. You can also cast Sanctuary without a slot during this time (details extend beyond the retrieved snippet).

name: College of Lore
flavor_text: Bards of the College of Lore know something about most things, collecting bits of knowledge from sources as diverse as scholarly tomes and peasant tales. Whether singing folk ballads in taverns or elaborate compositions in royal courts, these bards use their gifts to hold audiences spellbound. When the applause dies down, the audience members might find themselves questioning everything they held to be true, from their faith in the priesthood of the local temple to their loyalty to the king. The loyalty of these bards lies in the pursuit of beauty and truth, not in fealty to a monarch or following the tenets of a deity.
description: A knowledge-seeking bard who cuts deep with words, learns spells from any class, and can apply their vast expertise to any situation.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

features.name: Cutting Words (3rd Level)
features.description: When a creature within 60 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, or damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend a Bardic Inspiration use and subtract the roll from the creature's total.

features.name: Additional Magical Secrets (6th Level)
features.description: You learn two spells of your choice from any class. They must be of a level you can cast or a cantrip, and they count as bard spells for you but don't count against your number of bard spells known.

features.name: Peerless Skill (14th Level)
features.description: When you make an ability check, you can expend a Bardic Inspiration use and add the roll to your check. You can do so after rolling but before knowing the outcome.

name: College of Spirits
flavor_text: Bards of the College of Spirits seek tales with inherent power—be they legends, histories, or fictions—and bring their subjects to life. Using occult trappings, these bards become like leaders of a séance, weaving tales of creatures who have long since passed from the Material Plane. When these singers open their mouths, spirits speak through them.
description: A spirit-channeling bard who uses a Spiritual Focus to tell tales from beyond, producing a wide variety of magical effects drawn from a Spirit Tales table.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Guiding Whispers (3rd Level)
features.description: You learn the Guidance cantrip and can cast it at a range of up to 60 feet.

features.name: Spiritual Focus (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain a Spiritual Focus (candle, crystal ball, ouija board, tarokka deck, or skull). Starting at 6th level, when you cast a bard spell that deals damage or restores hit points through the focus, you can roll a d6 and add it to one roll of the spell.

features.name: Tales from Beyond (3rd Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can spend a Bardic Inspiration die to roll on the Spirit Tales table, producing an effect you can bestow on a target within 30 feet as an action. Effects range from temporary hit points and teleportation to psychic damage and area-of-effect blasts. You retain one tale at a time until you use it or finish a rest.

features.name: Spirit Session (6th Level)
features.description: You can conduct a 1-hour séance to contact spirits and learn a spell from any class (details extend beyond the retrieved snippet, but this feature allows you to temporarily learn a spell from another class list).

name: College of Swords
flavor_text: Bards of the College of Swords are called blades, and they entertain through daring feats of weapon prowess. Blades perform stunts such as sword swallowing, knife throwing and juggling, and mock combats. Beyond their careers as entertainers, blades are skilled warriors and frequently hire themselves out as mercenaries, assassins, or adventuring heroes.
description: A martial bard who turns blade mastery into an art. Blades gain a Fighting Style, use Blade Flourishes to control the battlefield, and can attack twice per action.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with medium armor and scimitars. If you are proficient with a simple or martial melee weapon, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your bard spells.

features.name: Fighting Style (3rd Level)
features.description: You adopt a Fighting Style: Dueling (+2 damage with a one-handed weapon and no other weapons) or Two-Weapon Fighting (add your ability modifier to the second attack's damage).

features.name: Blade Flourish (3rd Level)
features.description: When you take the Attack action and are not wearing heavy armor or using a shield, your walking speed increases by 10 feet, and when you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can use a Blade Flourish option: Defensive Flourish (extra damage and bonus to AC equal to the Bardic Inspiration roll), Slashing Flourish (extra damage to the target and another creature within 5 feet), or Mobile Flourish (extra damage and push the target up to 5 feet plus the roll). You can use one flourish per turn.

features.name: Extra Attack (6th Level)
features.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action. You can also cast a cantrip with a casting time of 1 action in place of one of those attacks. Master’s Flourish (14th Level): When you use a Blade Flourish, you can roll a d6 and use it instead of expending a Bardic Inspiration die.

name: College of Valor
flavor_text: Bards of the College of Valor are daring storytellers whose tales preserve the memory of the great heroes of the past. These bards sing the deeds of the mighty in vaulted halls or to crowds gathered around great bonfires. They travel to witness great events firsthand and to ensure that the memory of these events doesn't pass away. With their songs, they inspire new generations to reach the same heights of accomplishment as the heroes of old.
description: A martial bard who inspires allies in combat, gains proficiency with weapons and armor, can attack twice, and eventually weaves spellcasting and weapon strikes together seamlessly.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Combat Inspiration (3rd Level)
features.description: A creature with your Bardic Inspiration die can use it to add to its AC against an attack (Defense) or to the damage of an attack (Offense).

features.name: Martial Training (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and training with medium armor and shields. You can use a simple or martial weapon as a spellcasting focus for your bard spells.

features.name: Extra Attack (6th Level)
features.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action. You can also cast a cantrip with a casting time of 1 action in place of one of those attacks.

features.name: Battle Magic (14th Level)
features.description: After you cast a spell with a casting time of 1 action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

name: College of Whispers
flavor_text: Most folk are happy to welcome a bard into their midst. Bards of the College of Whispers use this to their advantage. They appear to be like any other bard, sharing news, singing songs, and telling tales to the audiences they gather. In truth, the College of Whispers teaches its students that they are wolves among sheep. These bards use their knowledge and magic to uncover secrets and turn them against others through extortion and threats. Many other bards hate the College of Whispers, viewing it as a parasite that uses the bards' reputation to acquire wealth and power.
description: A sinister, secret-stealing bard who turns weapon strikes into psychic assaults, terrorizes targets with whispered words, and steals the identities of the dead.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Psychic Blades (3rd Level)
features.description: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to deal an additional 2d6 psychic damage (3d6 at 5th, 5d6 at 10th, 8d6 at 15th level). You can do so only once per round on your turn.

features.name: Words of Terror (3rd Level)
features.description: If you speak to a humanoid alone for at least 1 minute, you can attempt to frighten it. At the end of the conversation, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of you or another creature of your choice for 1 hour. You must finish a rest before using this feature again.

features.name: Mantle of Whispers (6th Level)
features.description: When a humanoid dies within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to capture its shadow. As an action, you can transform the shadow into a disguise that makes you look like the dead person (healthy and alive) for 1 hour. You gain access to information the person would freely share with a casual acquaintance. You must finish a rest before capturing another shadow.

features.name: Shadow Lore (14th Level)
features.description: As an action, you whisper a phrase that only one creature within 30 feet can hear. It must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it is charmed by you for 8 hours or until you or your allies attack or damage it, interpreting your whispers as a description of its most mortifying secret. While charmed, it obeys your commands out of fear, though it won't risk its life for you. You must finish a long rest before using this feature again.

name: Knowledge Domain
flavor_text: "The gods of knowledge—including Oghma, Boccob, Gilean, Aureon, and Thoth—value learning and understanding above all. They promote the pursuit of knowledge and the gathering of lore. Some of these gods patronize sages and scholars, while others oversee hidden knowledge and secrets."
description: A domain focused on the pursuit and protection of knowledge. Clerics of this domain are scholars and seekers of truth, using their divine magic to uncover secrets and understand the world.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Blessings of Knowledge (1st Level)
features.description: You learn two languages of your choice. You also become proficient in your choice of two of the following skills: Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of those skills.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Knowledge of the Ages (2nd Level): As an action, you choose one skill or tool. For 10 minutes, you have proficiency with the chosen skill or tool.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Read Thoughts (6th Level): You can use your Channel Divinity to read a creature's thoughts. You can then use your access to the creature's mind to command it.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting (8th Level)
features.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

features.name: Visions of the Past (17th Level)
features.description: You can call up visions of the past that relate to an object you hold or your immediate surroundings. You spend at least 1 minute in meditation and prayer, then receive dreamlike, shadowy glimpses of recent events.

name: Life Domain
flavor_text: "The Life domain focuses on the vibrant positive energy—one of the fundamental forces of the universe—that sustains all life. The gods of life promote vitality and health through healing the sick and wounded, caring for those in need, and driving away the forces of death and undeath."
description: The masters of healing and restoration. Clerics of the Life Domain are often associated with agricultural deities, gods of healing or endurance, and gods of home and community. They are the ultimate support class, capable of restoring massive amounts of hit points and even bringing the dead back to life.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency (1st Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

features.name: Disciple of Life (1st Level)
features.description: Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Preserve Life (2nd Level): As an action, you present your holy symbol and evoke healing energy that can restore a number of hit points equal to five times your cleric level. Choose any creatures within 30 feet of you, and divide those hit points among them.

features.name: Blessed Healer (6th Level)
features.description: The healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. Immediately after you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Divine Strike (8th Level)
features.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage to the target.

features.name: Supreme Healing (17th Level)
features.description: When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die.

name: Light Domain
flavor_text: "Gods of light—including Helm, Lathander, Pholtus, Branchala, the Silver Flame, Belenus, Apollo, and Re-Horakhty—promote the ideals of rebirth and renewal, truth, vigilance, and beauty, often using the symbol of the sun. Clerics of a god of light are enlightened souls infused with radiance and the power of their gods’ discerning vision, charged with chasing away lies and burning away darkness."
description: A domain of blazing fire and revelation. Light Domain clerics wield the power of the sun, using radiant energy to sear their foes and reveal the truth. They are often associated with gods of truth, vigilance, beauty, insight, and renewal.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip (1st Level)
features.description: You gain the light cantrip if you don’t already know it.

features.name: Warding Flare (1st Level)
features.description: When you are attacked by a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, causing light to flare before the attacker before it hits or misses.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Radiance of the Dawn (2nd Level): As an action, you present your holy symbol, and any magical darkness within 30 feet of you is dispelled. Additionally, each hostile creature within 30 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature takes radiant damage equal to 2d10 + your cleric level on a failed saving throw, and half as much damage on a successful one.

features.name: Improved Flare (6th Level)
features.description: You can also use your Warding Flare feature when a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you attacks a creature other than you.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting (8th Level)
features.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

features.name: Corona of Light (17th Level)
features.description: You can use your action to activate an aura of sunlight that lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it using another action. You emit bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light 30 feet beyond that. Your enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saving throws against any spell that deals fire or radiant damage.

name: Nature Domain
flavor_text: "Gods of nature are as varied as the natural world itself, from inscrutable gods of the deep forests (such as Silvanus, Obad-Hai, Chislev, Balinor, and Pan) to friendly deities associated with particular springs and groves (such as Eldath)."
description: A domain for clerics who serve gods of nature. They act as champions of the wild, using their powers to protect the natural world and advance the interests of their nature deities.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Acolyte of Nature (1st Level)
features.description: You learn one cantrip of your choice from the druid spell list. You also gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Nature, or Survival.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency (1st Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Charm Animals and Plants (2nd Level): As an action, you present your holy symbol and invoke the name of your deity. Each beast or plant creature that can see you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw.

features.name: Dampen Elements (6th Level)
features.description: When you or a creature within 30 feet of you takes acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to grant resistance to the creature against that instance of the damage.

features.name: Divine Strike (8th Level)
features.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 cold, fire, or lightning damage (your choice) to the target.

features.name: Master of Nature (17th Level)
features.description: You gain the ability to command animals and plant creatures. While creatures are charmed by your Charm Animals and Plants feature, you can take a bonus action on your turn to verbally command what each of those creatures will do on its next turn.

name: Tempest Domain
flavor_text: "Gods whose portfolios include the Tempest domain—including Talos, Umberlee, Kord, Zeboim, the Devourer, Zeus, and Thor—govern storms, sea, and sky. They include gods of lightning and thunder, gods of earthquakes, some fire gods, and certain gods of violence, physical strength, and courage."
description: A domain of storm and destruction. Tempest clerics are conduits of divine wrath, using the power of lightning and thunder to bring balance to the world or to unleash devastation upon their foes.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies (1st Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

features.name: Wrath of the Storm (1st Level)
features.description: When a creature within 5 feet of you that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to cause the creature to make a Dexterity saving throw. The creature takes 2d8 lightning or thunder damage (your choice) on a failed saving throw, and half as much damage on a successful one.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Destructive Wrath (2nd Level): When you roll lightning or thunder damage, you can use your Channel Divinity to deal maximum damage, instead of rolling.

features.name: Thunderbolt Strike (6th Level)
features.description: When you deal lightning damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can also push it up to 10 feet away from you.

features.name: Divine Strike (8th Level)
features.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 thunder damage to the target.

features.name: Stormborn (17th Level)
features.description: You have a flying speed equal to your current walking speed whenever you are not underground or indoors.

name: Trickery Domain
flavor_text: "Gods of trickery—such as Tymora, Beshaba, Olidammara, the Traveler, Garl Glittergold, and Loki—are mischief-makers and instigators who stand as a constant challenge to the accepted order among both gods and mortals. They're patrons of thieves, scoundrels, gamblers, rebels, and liberators."
description: A domain of deception, illusion, and stealth. Clerics of the Trickery Domain are a disruptive force in the world, puncturing pride, mocking tyrants, freeing captives, and flouting hollow traditions. They prefer subterfuge and pranks to direct confrontation.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Blessing of the Trickster (1st Level)
features.description: You can use your action to touch a willing creature other than yourself to give it advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. This blessing lasts for 1 hour or until you use this feature again.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Invoke Duplicity (2nd Level): As an action, you create a perfect illusion of yourself that lasts for 1 minute, or until you lose your concentration. You can cast spells as though you were in the illusion's space, but you must use your own senses.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Cloak of Shadows (6th Level): As an action, you become invisible. You remain invisible until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Divine Strike (8th Level)
features.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 poison damage to the target.

features.name: Improved Duplicity (17th Level)
features.description: You can create up to four shadows of yourself with your Invoke Duplicity feature, instead of one.

name: War Domain
flavor_text: "Gods of war include champions of honor and chivalry (such as Torm, Heironeous, and Kiri-Jolith) as well as gods of destruction and pillage (such as Erythnul, the Fury, Gruumsh, and Ares) and gods of conquest and domination (such as Bane, Hextor, and Maglubiyet). Other war gods (such as Tempus, Nike, and Nuada) take a more neutral stance, promoting war in all its manifestations and supporting warriors in any situation."
description: A domain for clerics who excel in battle. They inspire others to fight the good fight or offer acts of violence as prayers. Gods of the War Domain watch over warriors and reward them for their great deeds.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies (1st Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

features.name: War Priest (1st Level)
features.description: Your god delivers bolts of inspiration to you while you are engaged in battle. When you use the Attack action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Guided Strike (2nd Level): You can use your Channel Divinity to strike with supernatural accuracy. When you make an attack roll, you can use your Channel Divinity to gain a +10 bonus to the roll. You can choose to do so after seeing the roll but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: War God's Blessing (6th Level): When a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to grant that creature a +10 bonus to the roll, using your Channel Divinity.

features.name: Divine Strike (8th Level)
features.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 damage of the same type dealt by the weapon to the target.

features.name: Avatar of Battle (17th Level)
features.description: You gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

name: Arcana Domain
flavor_text: "Magic suffuses the multiverse and fuels both destruction and creation. Clerics with this domain view magical knowledge not as power to be used in pursuit of personal ends, but as a gift they have the responsibility to share."
description: A domain for clerics who worship gods of magic. They know the secrets and potential of magic intimately and are often associated with knowledge. In the Realms, deities of this domain include Azuth, Mystra, and Corellon Larethian.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Arcane Initiate (1st Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency in the Arcana skill, and you gain two cantrips of your choice from the wizard spell list. For you, these cantrips count as cleric cantrips.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Arcane Abjuration (2nd Level): As an action, you present your holy symbol, and an aberrant, celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend of your choice that is within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw.

features.name: Spell Breaker (6th Level)
features.description: When you restore hit points to an ally with a spell of 1st level or higher, you can also end one spell of your choice on that creature. The level of the spell you end must be equal to or lower than the level of the spell slot you use to cast the healing spell.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting (8th Level)
features.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

features.name: Arcane Mastery (17th Level)
features.description: You choose four spells from the wizard spell list, one from each of the following levels: 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th. You add them to your list of domain spells. Like your other domain spells, they are always prepared and count as cleric spells for you.

name: Death Domain
flavor_text: "The Death domain is concerned with the forces that cause death, as well as the negative energy that gives rise to undead creatures. Deities such as the Raven Queen, Hel, Hades, Anubis, and Osiris are patrons of this domain."
description: A domain that deals with the end of life and the power of undeath. Clerics of this domain are masters of necrotic energy and can drain the life force from their foes. They are often villainous, but some serve as grim shepherds of the dead.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency (1st Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons.

features.name: Reaper (1st Level)
features.description: You learn one necromancy cantrip of your choice from any spell list. When you cast a necromancy cantrip that normally targets only one creature, the spell can instead target two creatures within range and within 5 feet of each other.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Touch of Death (2nd Level): When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can use your Channel Divinity to deal extra necrotic damage to the target, equal to 5 + twice your cleric level.

features.name: Inescapable Destruction (6th Level)
features.description: Starting at 6th level, your ability to channel negative energy becomes more potent. Necrotic damage dealt by your cleric spells and Channel Divinity options ignores resistance to necrotic damage.

features.name: Divine Strike (8th Level)
features.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage to the target.

features.name: Improved Reaper (17th Level)
features.description: When you cast a necromancy spell of 1st through 5th level that targets only one creature, the spell can instead target two creatures within range and within 5 feet of each other.

name: Forge Domain
flavor_text: "Clerics of the forge believe that the act of creation is an act of faith. They see the forge as a sacred place, and they believe that the gods of the forge—such as Gond, Reorx, Onatar, Moradin, Hephaestus, and Goibhniu—bless those who work with their hands and create things of beauty and utility."
description: The domain of crafters and smiths. Forge Domain clerics are masters of creating and enhancing equipment. They can imbue weapons and armor with magical properties, and they are highly durable, gaining resistance to fire and a bonus to AC.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies (1st Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.

features.name: Blessing of the Forge (1st Level)
features.description: At the end of a long rest, you can touch one nonmagical object that is a suit of armor or a simple or martial weapon. Until the end of your next long rest or until you die, the object becomes a magic item, granting a +1 bonus to AC if it's armor or a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls if it's a weapon.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Artisan's Blessing (2nd Level): You can use your Channel Divinity to create simple items. You conduct an hour-long ritual that crafts a nonmagical item that must include some metal: a simple or martial weapon, a suit of armor, ten pieces of ammunition, a set of tools, or another metal object.

features.name: Soul of the Forge (6th Level)
features.description: You gain resistance to fire damage. While wearing heavy armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

features.name: Divine Strike (8th Level)
features.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 fire damage to the target.

features.name: Saint of Forge and Fire (17th Level)
features.description: Your blessed affinity with fire and metal becomes more powerful. You gain immunity to fire damage. While wearing heavy armor, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

name: Grave Domain
flavor_text: "The Grave Domain concerns itself with the boundary between life and death. Gods of the grave—such as the Raven Queen, Kelemvor, Wee Jas, Hades, and Anubis—watch over the transition from life to death, ensuring that the natural order is not disrupted."
description: A domain for clerics who stand at the line between life and death. Unlike Death Domain clerics, who seek to inflict or pervert death, Grave Domain clerics seek to maintain the natural cycle, ensuring that the dead stay dead and that the living are protected from undeath.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Circle of Mortality (1st Level)
features.description: You gain the ability to manipulate the balance between life and death. You learn the spare the dying cantrip. When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell to a creature at 0 hit points, you instead use the highest number possible for each die.

features.name: Eyes of the Grave (1st Level)
features.description: As an action, you can open your awareness to magically detect the presence of undead. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any undead within 60 feet of you that isn't behind total cover and that isn't protected from divination magic.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Path to the Grave (2nd Level): As an action, you choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you, cursing it until the end of your next turn. The next time you or an ally of yours hits the cursed creature with an attack, the creature has vulnerability to all of that attack's damage, and then the curse ends.

features.name: Sentinel at Death's Door (6th Level)
features.description: As a reaction when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you suffers a critical hit, you can turn that attack into a normal hit. Any effects triggered by a critical hit are canceled.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting (8th Level)
features.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

features.name: Keeper of Souls (17th Level)
features.description: When an enemy you can see dies within 60 feet of you, you or one ally of your choice that is within 60 feet of you regains hit points equal to the enemy's number of Hit Dice. You can use this feature only if you aren't incapacitated, and you can use it a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Order Domain
flavor_text: "The Order Domain represents discipline, as well as devotion to the laws that govern a society, an institution, or a philosophy. Clerics of Order meditate on logic and justice as they serve their gods, who embody the ideals of law and order."
description: A domain of law and hierarchy. Order Domain clerics are disciplined and logical, using their divine magic to enforce the rules of their god and maintain the social order. They can charm or control enemies and even regain spent spell slots.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies (1st Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor. You also gain proficiency in the Intimidation or Persuasion skill (your choice).

features.name: Voice of Authority (1st Level)
features.description: If you cast a spell with a spell slot of 1st level or higher and target an ally with the spell, that ally can use their reaction immediately after the spell to make one weapon attack against a creature of your choice that you can see.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Order's Demand (2nd Level): As an action, you present your holy symbol, and each creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you until the end of your next turn or until you or your allies deal damage to the charmed creature. You can also cause any of the charmed creatures to drop what they are holding when they fail the saving throw.

features.name: Embodiment of the Law (6th Level)
features.description: You can cast spells of 1st level or higher that have a casting time of 1 action as a bonus action, provided you use a spell slot of 2nd level or higher.

features.name: Divine Strike (8th Level)
features.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 psychic damage to the target.

features.name: Order's Wrath (17th Level)
features.description: Enemies you designate as the targets of your Order's Demand feature have vulnerability to all damage from your Divine Strike feature. This vulnerability lasts until the end of your next turn.

name: Peace Domain
flavor_text: "Clerics of the Peace Domain preside over the signing of treaties, and they are often asked to arbitrate in disputes. These clerics' blessings draw people together and help them shoulder one another's burdens, and the clerics' magic aids those who are driven to fight for the way of peace."
description: A domain for clerics who seek to resolve conflicts and bring people together. They are versatile support classes, using their powers to bond allies, heal wounds, and protect the innocent. They prioritize compromise over violence but are still formidable on the battlefield.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Implement of Peace (1st Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency in the Insight, Performance, or Persuasion skill (your choice).

features.name: Emboldening Bond (1st Level)
features.description: You can forge a magical bond between two or more creatures. As an action, choose a number of willing creatures within 30 feet of you, up to a number equal to your proficiency bonus. You create a magical bond among them for 10 minutes or until you use this feature again. While any bonded creature is within 30 feet of another, the creature can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw it makes. Each creature can add the d4 no more than once per turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Balm of Peace (2nd Level): As an action, you can use your Channel Divinity to make your very presence a soothing balm. You can move up to your speed, without provoking opportunity attacks, and when you move within 5 feet of any other creature during this action, you can restore a number of hit points to that creature equal to 2d6 + your Wisdom modifier. A creature can benefit from this feature only once per turn.

features.name: Protective Bond (6th Level)
features.description: The bond you forge between people helps them protect each other. When a creature affected by your Emboldening Bond feature is about to take damage, a second bonded creature within 30 feet of the first can use its reaction to teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the first creature and take the damage instead. This damage cannot be reduced in any way.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting (8th Level)
features.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

features.name: Expansive Bond (17th Level)
features.description: The benefits of your Emboldening Bond and Protective Bond features now work when the creatures are within 60 feet of each other. Additionally, when a creature uses Protective Bond to take someone else's damage, the creature has resistance to that damage.

name: Twilight Domain
flavor_text: "The twilit transition from light into darkness often brings calm and even joy, as the day’s labors end and the hours of rest begin. Clerics of the Twilight Domain worship deities that command the night and guide mortals between the hours of dawn and dusk as they drift off to sleep. They are the protectors of the night, offering shelter and comfort in the darkness."
description: A domain of twilight and protection. Twilight Domain clerics are guardians of the night, using their powers to shield their allies from harm, provide them with darkvision, and even grant them the ability to fly. They are a powerful support class, especially in campaigns that involve travel or combat in the dark.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies (1st Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

features.name: Eyes of Night (1st Level)
features.description: You can see through the deepest gloom. You have darkvision out to a range of 300 feet. In that radius, you can see in dim light as if it were bright light and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can share this darkvision with a number of willing creatures equal to your proficiency bonus, and it lasts for 1 hour.

features.name: Vigilant Blessing (1st Level)
features.description: As an action, you give a creature you touch advantage on the next initiative roll it makes. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: Twilight Sanctuary (2nd Level): As an action, you present your holy symbol, and a sphere of twilight emanates from you. The sphere is centered on you, has a 30-foot radius, and is filled with dim light. You and any creature of your choice in the sphere are granted temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + your cleric level at the end of each of your turns. You can also end one effect on a creature in the sphere that is causing it to be charmed or frightened. The sphere lasts for 1 minute or until you are incapacitated or die.

features.name: Steps of Night (6th Level)
features.description: You can draw on the mystical power of night to rise into the air. As a bonus action when you are in dim light or darkness, you can magically give yourself a flying speed equal to your walking speed for 1 minute. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Divine Strike (8th Level)
features.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage to the target.

features.name: Twilight Shroud (17th Level)
features.description: The twilight that you summon offers a protective embrace: you and your allies have half cover while in the sphere created by your Twilight Sanctuary feature.

name: Circle of Dreams
flavor_text: "Druids of the Circle of Dreams hail from regions that have strong ties to the Feywild and its dreamlike realms. The druids’ goodwill and connection to that place make them beloved by the good-aligned fey. These druids seek to fill the world with dreamy wonder. Their magic mends wounds and brings joy to downcast hearts, and the realms they protect are gleaming, fruitful places, where dream and reality blur together."
description: A support-oriented druid tied to the Feywild, acting as a guardian of rest and a powerful healer. You gain a pool of fey energy to heal at range, can create a magically concealed haven for your party, teleport short distances, and eventually walk through dreams themselves.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Balm of the Summer Court (2nd Level)
features.description: You gain a pool of fey energy represented by a number of d6s equal to your druid level. As a bonus action, you can choose one creature you can see within 120 feet and expend one or more of these dice to heal it, granting additional temporary hit points equal to the number of dice spent. You can spend a number of dice equal to half your druid level at once, and you regain all expended dice on a long rest.

features.name: Hearth of Moonlight and Shadow (6th Level)
features.description: During a short or long rest, you can summon an invisible 30-foot-radius sphere of protection. Creatures inside gain a +5 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) and Wisdom (Perception) checks, and open flames within the sphere do not cast light outside of it.

features.name: Hidden Paths (10th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, or teleport one willing creature you touch up to 30 feet. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining all uses on a long rest.

features.name: Walker in Dreams (14th Level)
features.description: After a short rest, you can cast one of the following spells without expending a spell slot or material components: Dream, Scrying, or Teleportation Circle. If you cast Teleportation Circle this way, it opens a portal to the last location where you finished a long rest. Once used, this feature cannot be used again until you finish a long rest.

name: Circle of the Land
flavor_text: "The Circle of the Land is made up of mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites through a vast oral tradition. These druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle’s wisest members preside as the chief priests of communities that hold to the Old Faith and serve as advisors to the rulers of those folk. As a member of this circle, your magic is influenced by the land where you were initiated into the circle’s mysterious rites."
description: The quintessential spellcasting druid. Your connection to a specific terrain type grants you bonus spells, and you can recover expended spell slots on a short rest, giving you remarkable longevity as a caster.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip (2nd Level)
features.description: You learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice. It doesn't count against your number of druid cantrips known.

features.name: Natural Recovery (2nd Level)
features.description: During a short rest, you can recover expended spell slots with a combined level equal to or less than half your druid level (rounded up). None of the recovered slots can be 6th level or higher. You must finish a long rest before using this feature again.

features.name: Circle Spells (3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th Level)
