features.description: You gain a bonus to any Charisma check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1). You also gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Deception, Performance, or Persuasion.

features.name: Beguiling Twist (7th Level)
features.description: The magic of the Feywild guards your mind. You have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the charmed or frightened condition. In addition, whenever you or a creature you can see within 120 feet of you succeeds on a saving throw against being charmed or frightened, you can use your reaction to force a different creature you can see within 120 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, or be charmed or frightened by you for 1 minute.

features.name: Fey Reinforcements (11th Level)
features.description: You can cast Summon Fey without a material component and without using a spell slot. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

features.name: Misty Wanderer (15th Level)
features.description: You can cast Misty Step without using a spell slot a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier per long rest. Additionally, whenever you cast Misty Step, you can bring one willing creature of your size or smaller within 5 feet of you along with you.

name: Swarmkeeper
flavor_text: "Feeling a deep connection to the environment around them, some rangers reach out through their magical connection to the world and bond with a swarm of nature spirits."
description: You are a Ranger who has bonded with a swarm of nature spirits. This swarm is a potent force that can harry your foes, protect you from harm, and even lift you into the air. You are never truly alone, and your connection to the natural world is made manifest in a tangible, buzzing, and biting cloud of allies.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Gathered Swarm (3rd Level)
features.description: Once on each of your turns, immediately after you hit a creature with an attack, you can cause your swarm to assist you in one of the following ways: The target takes an extra 1d6 piercing damage from the swarm. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be moved by the swarm up to 15 feet horizontally in a direction of your choice. You are moved by the swarm 5 feet horizontally in a direction of your choice.

features.name: Swarmkeeper Magic (3rd Level)
features.description: You learn the Mage Hand cantrip, which takes the form of your swarming nature spirits. You also learn additional spells at higher levels as shown on the Swarmkeeper Spells table.

features.name: Writhing Tide (7th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can gain a flying speed of 10 feet and hover for 1 minute. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

features.name: Mighty Swarm (11th Level)
features.description: Your Gathered Swarm grows mightier. The damage increases to 1d8. If a creature fails its save against being moved, you can also knock it prone. When you are moved by the swarm, you gain half cover until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Swarming Dispersal (15th Level)
features.description: When you take damage, you can use your reaction to gain resistance to that damage. You then vanish into your swarm and teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

name: Drakewarden
flavor_text: "Drakewardens are rangers who use their magical connection with nature to form an enduring bond with a minor dragon, a drake. This bond allows the ranger to summon the drake to their side and to share in the awe-inspiring power wielded by dragons."
description: You are a Ranger who has forged a mystical bond with a drake, a lesser dragon. This companion fights by your side, and as you grow in power, so too does your drake, eventually allowing you to ride it, share its elemental nature, and unleash its draconic fury upon your enemies.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Draconic Gift (3rd Level)
features.description: You learn to speak, read, and write Draconic if you can't already. You also learn the Thaumaturgy cantrip, which is a ranger spell for you.

features.name: Drake Companion (3rd Level)
features.description: You form a primal bond with a drake, represented by a physical token. You can use an action to summon your drake, which obeys your commands and fights alongside you. It shares your initiative and takes its turn immediately after yours.

features.name: Bond of Fang and Scale (7th Level)
features.description: Your bond with your drake deepens, granting you both new abilities (specific details are not present in the search snippets).

features.name: Drake's Breath (11th Level)
features.description: As an action, you can exhale a 30-foot cone of damaging breath, or you can cause your drake to exhale it. The damage type is determined by your drake's Draconic Essence.

features.name: Perfected Bond (15th Level)
features.description: Your drake grows to Large size, and you gain the ability to ride it. You also gain other unspecified benefits that perfect your bond.

name: Thief
flavor_text: You excel at climbing, sneaking, and stealing, using your agility and cunning to gain access to places others can’t go.
description: The archetypal rogue, a master of stealth, larceny, and acrobatic movement. Thieves are unmatched at infiltration, picking pockets, and using magic items.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Fast Hands (3rd Level)
features.description: You can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thieves’ tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.

features.name: Second-Story Work (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement. You can also make a running jump with only a 5-foot start.

features.name: Supreme Sneak (9th Level)
features.description: You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

features.name: Use Magic Device (13th Level)
features.description: You ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items. Thief’s Reflexes (17th Level): You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10.

name: Assassin
flavor_text: You focus your training on the grim art of death. Those who adhere to this archetype are diverse: hired killers, spies, bounty hunters, and even specially anointed priests trained to exterminate the enemies of their deity.
description: An expert of ambush and disguise, the Assassin is a master of dealing death from the shadows. You excel at infiltrating, impersonating others, and delivering devastating strikes before a foe can react.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with the disguise kit and the poisoner’s kit.

features.name: Assassinate (3rd Level)
features.description: You have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn’t taken a turn in the combat yet. Any hit you score against a surprised creature is a critical hit.

features.name: Infiltration Expertise (9th Level)
features.description: You can unfailingly create false identities for yourself. You spend seven days and 25 gp to establish a false identity, after which you can convincingly pass yourself off as that person.

features.name: Impostor (13th Level)
features.description: You gain the ability to unerringly mimic another person’s speech, writing, and behavior, provided you have spent at least three hours studying them.

features.name: Death Strike (17th Level)
features.description: When you attack and hit a creature that is surprised, it must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier). On a failed save, double the damage of your attack against the creature.

name: Arcane Trickster
flavor_text: Some rogues enhance their fine-honed skills of stealth and agility with spells, learning magical tricks to aid them in their trade.
description: A rogue who blends stealth and trickery with arcane magic. You use illusions and enchantments to distract and deceive, and you can use your mage hand to perform larcenous acts at a distance.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Spellcasting (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain the ability to cast spells. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability. You know three wizard cantrips and three 1st-level wizard spells, learning more as you gain levels. You favor spells from the illusion and enchantment schools.

features.name: Mage Hand Legerdemain (3rd Level)
features.description: You can cast mage hand and make the spectral hand invisible. You can use it to stow or retrieve objects, pick locks, or disarm traps at a distance.

features.name: Magical Ambush (9th Level)
features.description: If you are hidden from a creature when you cast a spell on it, it has disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against the spell this turn.

features.name: Versatile Trickster (13th Level)
features.description: You gain the ability to distract targets with your mage hand, giving you advantage on attack rolls against that creature until the end of the turn.

features.name: Spell Thief (17th Level)
features.description: You gain the ability to steal the knowledge of how to cast a spell from another spellcaster. If a creature casts a spell that targets you, you can use your reaction to force it to make a saving throw; on a failure, you negate the spell’s effect and steal it, gaining the ability to cast it yourself.

name: Inquisitive
flavor_text: You rely on your sharp eye for detail and your ability to read others. Your insight and intuition allow you to unravel secrets and see through deception.
description: A master detective and interrogator. Inquisitives rely on keen observation and insight to find weaknesses, whether in a locked room or an opponent’s fighting style.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Ear for Deceit (3rd Level)
features.description: Whenever you make a Wisdom (Insight) check to determine if a creature is lying, treat a roll of 7 or lower on the d20 as an 8.

features.name: Eye for Detail (3rd Level)
features.description: You can use a bonus action to make a Wisdom (Perception) check to spot a hidden creature or object, or to make an Intelligence (Investigation) check to uncover or decipher clues.

features.name: Insightful Fighting (3rd Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can make a Wisdom (Insight) check against a creature’s Charisma (Deception) check. If you succeed, you can use your Sneak Attack against that target even if you don’t have advantage, as long as you don’t have disadvantage.

features.name: Steady Eye (9th Level)
features.description: You have advantage on any Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

features.name: Unerring Eye (13th Level)
features.description: Your instincts are so honed that you can sense the presence of illusions, shapechangers, and other magic designed to deceive the senses. As an action, you can sense such effects within 30 feet of you.

features.name: Eye for Weakness (17th Level)
features.description: You learn to exploit the weaknesses of your foes. When you use Insightful Fighting, you can choose to deal an extra 3d6 damage to the target on your next Sneak Attack against it before the end of your next turn.

name: Mastermind
flavor_text: Your focus is on people and on the influence and secrets they trade. Many spies, courtiers, and schemers follow this archetype, leading lives of intrigue.
description: A cunning tactician and manipulator. The Mastermind excels at social manipulation, using their sharp mind to aid allies and deceive foes.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Master of Intrigue (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with the disguise kit, the forgery kit, and one gaming set of your choice. You also learn two languages of your choice.

features.name: Master of Tactics (3rd Level)
features.description: You can use the Help action as a bonus action. When you use the Help action to aid an ally in attacking a creature, the target can be within 30 feet of you, rather than 5 feet, if the ally can hear you.

features.name: Insightful Manipulator (9th Level)
features.description: If you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside of combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own.

features.name: Misdirection (13th Level)
features.description: You can sometimes cause another creature to suffer an attack meant for you. When you are targeted by an attack while a creature within 5 feet of you is granting you cover, you can use your reaction to have the attack target that creature instead of you.

features.name: Soul of Deceit (17th Level)
features.description: Your thoughts can’t be read by telepathy or other means, unless you allow it. You can present false thoughts by making a Charisma (Deception) check contested by the mind reader’s Wisdom (Insight) check. You can also magically alter your voice and appearance, as per a disguise self spell, at will.

name: Scout
flavor_text: You are skilled in stealth and surviving in the wilds, focusing on mobility and awareness.
description: A mobile skirmisher and expert wilderness survivor. The Scout is difficult to pin down in a fight and can navigate natural environments with ease.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Skirmisher (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency in the Nature and Survival skills if you don’t already have it. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of those proficiencies.

features.name: Survivalist (3rd Level)
features.description: You can move up to half your speed as a reaction when an enemy ends its turn within 5 feet of you. This movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks.

features.name: Superior Mobility (9th Level)
features.description: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet. If you have a climb speed or a swim speed, they also increase by 10 feet.

features.name: Ambush Master (13th Level)
features.description: You have advantage on initiative rolls. Additionally, the first creature you hit during the first round of a combat has advantage on the next attack roll made against it by one of your allies.

features.name: Sudden Strike (17th Level)
features.description: You can strike with deadly speed. If you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make one additional attack as a bonus action. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a short or long rest.

name: Swashbuckler
flavor_text: You focus your training on the art of the blade, relying on speed, elegance, and charm in equal parts.
description: A flashy and charismatic duelist. The Swashbuckler excels in one-on-one combat, using their panache to charm foes and their agility to strike with deadly precision.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Fancy Footwork (3rd Level)
features.description: During your turn, if you make a melee attack against a creature, that creature can’t make opportunity attacks against you for the rest of your turn.

features.name: Rakish Audacity (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Charisma modifier. You also gain an additional way to use your Sneak Attack: you don’t need advantage on the attack roll if you are within 5 feet of the target, no other creatures are within 5 feet of you, and you don’t have disadvantage on the attack roll.

features.name: Panache (9th Level)
features.description: Your charm is so potent it can sway others. As an action, you can make a Charisma (Persuasion) check contested by a creature’s Wisdom (Insight) check. If you succeed, the creature is charmed by you for 1 minute. While charmed, it regards you as a friendly acquaintance. If the creature is hostile, it instead has disadvantage on attack rolls against creatures other than you.

features.name: Elegant Maneuver (13th Level)
features.description: You can use a bonus action on your turn to gain advantage on the next Dexterity (Acrobatics) or Strength (Athletics) check you make during the same turn.

features.name: Master Duelist (17th Level)
features.description: Your mastery of the blade lets you turn failure into success in combat. If you miss with an attack roll, you can roll it again with advantage. Once you do so, you can’t use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Phantom
flavor_text: Echoes of those who have died cling to you. You can learn to channel the power of the departed, using their knowledge and essence to fuel your own abilities.
description: A rogue who taps into the power of death and the spirits of the dead. Phantoms can gain knowledge from the departed, capture souls, and even take on a ghostly form.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Whispers of the Dead (3rd Level)
features.description: Whenever you finish a short or long rest, you can choose one skill or tool proficiency that you lack and gain it, as a ghostly presence shares its knowledge with you. This benefit lasts until your next rest.

features.name: Wails from the Grave (3rd Level)
features.description: Immediately after you deal your Sneak Attack damage to a creature on your turn, you can target a second creature that you can see within 30 feet of the first creature. Roll half the number of Sneak Attack dice for your level (rounded up). The second creature takes psychic damage equal to the roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.

features.name: Tokens of the Departed (9th Level)
features.description: When a creature you can see dies within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to capture its soul in a Tiny trinket. You can have a number of soul trinkets equal to your proficiency bonus. You can use a soul trinket to gain advantage on a death saving throw, or to fuel your Wails from the Grave feature without expending a use.

features.name: Ghost Walk (13th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can assume a ghostly form for 10 minutes. While in this form, you gain a flying speed of 10 feet, can hover, and can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. You also have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. You can use this feature once per long rest. Death’s Friend (17th Level): Your connection to death is so strong that you can momentarily cheat it. When you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to instead drop to 1 hit point. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Soulknife
flavor_text: A Soulknife strikes and infiltrates with the mind, cutting through barriers both physical and psychic. These rogues discover psionic power within themselves and channel it to do their roguish work.
description: A rogue who manifests blades of psychic energy. Soulknives are masters of stealth and infiltration, using their psionic abilities to enhance their skills, communicate telepathically, and strike directly at the minds of their foes.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Psionic Power (3rd Level)
features.description: You gain a wellspring of psionic energy within yourself. You have a number of Psionic Energy dice (starting as d6s) equal to twice your proficiency bonus. You can spend these dice to fuel your psionic abilities. You regain all expended dice on a long rest.

features.name: Psychic Blades (3rd Level)
features.description: You can manifest shimmering blades of psychic energy in your empty hands. You can use these blades to make melee or ranged weapon attacks. On a hit, they deal psychic damage equal to 1d6 plus the ability modifier you used for the attack roll. After you attack with a blade, you can make a second attack with a different blade as a bonus action if your other hand is free.

features.name: Soul Blades (9th Level)
features.description: Your Psychic Blades are now an extension of your being. You can use them to deliver precise strikes. When you make an attack with a Psychic Blade, you can expend a Psionic Energy die to add it to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you can expend a die to add it to the damage roll. You can also use your blades to teleport short distances.

features.name: Psychic Veil (13th Level)
features.description: You can weave a veil of psychic static to mask yourself. As an action, you can become invisible for 1 hour, or until you attack, deal damage, or force a creature to make a saving throw. You can use this feature once per long rest.

features.name: Rend Mind (17th Level)
features.description: You can sweep your Psychic Blades directly through a creature’s mind. When you use your Psychic Blades to deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier). On a failed save, the creature is stunned for 1 minute. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. You can use this feature once per long rest.

name: Draconic Bloodline
flavor_text: "Your innate magic comes from draconic magic that was mingled with your blood or that of your ancestors. Most often, sorcerers with this origin trace their descent back to a mighty sorcerer of ancient times who made a bargain with a dragon or who might even have claimed a dragon parent."
description: The archetypal "dragon sorcerer." You gain physical traits of your draconic ancestor, including scaled skin, extra durability, and eventually wings. Your magic is tied to a specific elemental damage type determined by your dragon ancestry, which you can enhance and eventually project as an aura of awe or fear.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Dragon Ancestor (1st Level)
features.description: Choose one type of dragon (e.g., Black/Acid, Blue/Lightning, Red/Fire, White/Cold). You can speak, read, and write Draconic, and your proficiency bonus is doubled on Charisma checks when interacting with dragons.

features.name: Draconic Resilience (1st Level)
features.description: Your hit point maximum increases by 1 and by 1 again whenever you gain a Sorcerer level. When not wearing armor, your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier.

features.name: Elemental Affinity (6th Level)
features.description: When you cast a spell that deals damage of your draconic ancestry's type, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll. You can also spend 1 sorcery point to gain resistance to that damage type for 1 hour.

features.name: Dragon Wings (14th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can sprout a pair of dragon wings from your back, gaining a flying speed equal to your current speed. They last until you dismiss them.

features.name: Draconic Presence (18th Level)
features.description: As an action, spend 5 sorcery points to exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to 60 feet for 1 minute (concentration). Hostile creatures starting their turn in the aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed (awe) or frightened (fear).

name: Wild Magic
flavor_text: "Your innate magic stems from the forces of chaos that underlie the order of creation. You or an ancestor might have endured exposure to raw, uncontrolled magic, or you might have been born during a magical catastrophe."
description: A sorcerer whose magic is volatile and unpredictable. Your spellcasting can trigger random magical effects from a surge table, and you can manipulate probability itself. The subclass is defined by chaos, risk, and the thrill of a lucky (or unlucky) roll.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Wild Magic Surge (1st Level)
features.description: Once per turn, immediately after you cast a Sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, you can roll 1d20. On a 20, you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table to create a random magical effect.

features.name: Tides of Chaos (1st Level)
features.description: You can give yourself advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw before you roll the d20. Once you do so, you must cast a Sorcerer spell with a spell slot or finish a long rest before using it again. If you cast a spell before resting, you automatically roll on the Wild Magic Surge table.

features.name: Bend Luck (6th Level)
features.description: When another creature makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use your reaction and spend 2 sorcery points to roll 1d4 and apply it as a bonus or penalty to the creature's roll.

features.name: Controlled Chaos (14th Level)
features.description: Whenever you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table, you can roll twice and use either result.

features.name: Spell Bombardment (18th Level)
features.description: When you roll damage for a spell and roll the highest number possible on any of the dice, you can roll that die again and add it to the damage. You can use this once per turn.

name: Divine Soul
flavor_text: "Your innate magic springs from a divine source—a blessing from a god, a powerful ancestor, or a cosmic event that infused you with holy power. Your magic is a gift, a manifestation of the divine will that flows through your veins."
description: A sorcerer with a spark of divine magic. You gain access to the entire Cleric spell list, allowing you to heal, support, and blast with equal proficiency. You are a bridge between the arcane and the divine, able to manipulate fate and sprout spectral wings.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Divine Magic (1st Level)
features.description: You learn spells from the Cleric spell list, which count as Sorcerer spells for you. You also gain one additional spell based on your affinity (Good, Evil, Law, Chaos, or Neutrality), which does not count against your spells known.

features.name: Favored by the Gods (1st Level)
features.description: If you fail a saving throw or miss with an attack roll, you can roll 2d4 and add it to the roll, potentially turning a failure into a success. Once used, you must finish a short or long rest to use it again.

features.name: Empowered Healing (6th Level)
features.description: Once per turn when you or a creature within 5 feet of you casts a healing spell, you can spend 1 sorcery point to reroll a number of the healing dice (up to your Charisma modifier) and use the new rolls.

features.name: Otherworldly Wings (14th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can manifest a pair of spectral wings from your back, gaining a flying speed of 30 feet. The wings last until you are incapacitated, die, or dismiss them.

features.name: Unearthly Recovery (18th Level)
features.description: If you have half your hit points or fewer, you can use an action to regain a number of hit points equal to half your hit point maximum. Once used, you must finish a long rest to use it again.

name: Shadow Magic
flavor_text: "You are a creature of shadow, for your innate magic comes from the Shadowfell itself. You might trace your lineage to an entity from that place, or perhaps you were exposed to its foul magic and emerged changed."
description: A sorcerer who draws power from the Plane of Shadow. You gain darkvision, can see through magical darkness, and can summon a shadow hound to harry your foes. You become a master of stealth and survival, eventually transforming into an umbral form.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Eyes of the Dark (1st Level)
features.description: You gain darkvision out to 120 feet. Starting at 3rd level, you can cast the Darkness spell using sorcery points. If you spend 2 sorcery points when you cast it, you can see through the magical darkness.

features.name: Strength of the Grave (1st Level)
features.description: When damage reduces you to 0 hit points, you can make a Charisma saving throw (DC 5 + the damage taken). On a success, you drop to 1 hit point instead. Once used, you must finish a long rest to use it again.

features.name: Hound of Ill Omen (6th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can spend 3 sorcery points to summon a shadow hound (using Dire Wolf statistics) that targets a creature of your choice. While the hound is within 5 feet of the target, the target has disadvantage on saving throws against your spells.

features.name: Shadow Walk (14th Level)
features.description: While in dim light or darkness, you can use a bonus action to teleport up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or darkness.

features.name: Umbral Form (18th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can spend 6 sorcery points to transform yourself into a shadowy form for 1 minute. In this form, you have resistance to all damage except force and radiant, and you can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain.

name: Storm Sorcery
flavor_text: "Your innate magic comes from the power of elemental air. Many with this power can trace their magic back to a near-death experience caused by the Great Rain, but perhaps you were born during a howling gale so powerful that folk still tell stories of it, or your lineage might include the influence of potent air creatures such as vaati or djinn."
description: A sorcerer infused with the raw power of the storm. You can speak Primordial, fly short distances after casting spells, resist lightning and thunder, and eventually gain a permanent flying speed. You are a mobile, elemental blaster.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Wind Speaker (1st Level)
features.description: You can speak, read, and write Primordial, and you can communicate with creatures that speak its dialects (Aquan, Auran, Ignan, and Terran).

features.name: Tempestuous Magic (1st Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, immediately before or after you cast a spell of 1st level or higher, you can fly up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

features.name: Heart of the Storm (6th Level)
features.description: You gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that deals lightning or thunder damage, creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you take lightning or thunder damage equal to half your Sorcerer level.

features.name: Storm Guide (6th Level)
features.description: You can subtly control the weather around you. You can stop rain in a 20-foot radius or choose the direction of the wind in a 100-foot radius.

features.name: Storm's Fury (14th Level)
features.description: When a creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal lightning damage equal to your Sorcerer level to the attacker, and it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 20 feet away.

features.name: Wind Soul (18th Level)
features.description: You gain immunity to lightning and thunder damage and a magical flying speed of 60 feet. You can also use an action to reduce your flying speed to 30 feet for 1 hour and grant a flying speed of 30 feet to a number of creatures within 30 feet equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier.

name: Stone Sorcery
flavor_text: "Your magic springs from a mystical link between your soul and the magic of elemental earth. You might trace a distant ancestor to the Plane of Earth, or your family might have earned a mighty boon in return for a service to the dao lords."
description: A gish-style sorcerer with a connection to earth and stone. Unlike most sorcerers, you gain proficiency with shields, simple weapons, and martial weapons, allowing you to wade into melee. You gain extra durability, a stony AC calculation, and the ability to protect allies with a Stone Aegis and teleport to their defense.
dm_guidelines: This subclass originated in Unearthed Arcana (UA) and is not official published material. It is presented as homebrew/playtest content.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies (1st Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with shields, simple weapons, and martial weapons.

features.name: Metal Magic (1st Level)
features.description: When you learn a Sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, you can choose it from an expanded list of smite and weapon-enhancing spells (e.g., compelled duel, searing smite, branding smite).

features.name: Stone's Durability (1st Level)
features.description: Your hit point maximum increases by 1 and by 1 again whenever you gain a Sorcerer level. As an action, you can gain a base AC of 13 + your Constitution modifier if you aren't wearing armor, and your skin assumes a stony appearance.

features.name: Stone Aegis (6th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can grant a protective aegis to an allied creature within 60 feet. The target reduces bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage by 2 + (your Sorcerer level ÷ 4). When a creature hits the protected target with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to teleport within 5 feet of the attacker and make a melee weapon attack that deals an extra 1d10 force damage (increasing to 2d10 at 11th and 3d10 at 17th level).

features.name: Stone's Edge (14th Level)
features.description: When you cast a spell that deals damage, choose one creature damaged by it. That creature takes extra force damage equal to half your Sorcerer level.

features.name: Earth Master's Aegis (18th Level)
features.description: When you use Stone Aegis, you can choose up to three creatures to gain its benefits.

name: Aberrant Mind
flavor_text: "An alien influence has wrapped its tendrils around your mind, giving you psionic power. You can now touch other minds with that power and alter the world around you by using it to control the magical energy of the multiverse."
description: A psionic sorcerer whose mind has been touched by an alien entity. You gain telepathy, can cast spells without verbal or somatic components by spending sorcery points, resist psychic damage, and can physically transform your body with aberrant traits.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Telepathic Speech (1st Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can form a telepathic connection with one creature you can see within 30 feet. You can speak telepathically with each other while within a number of miles equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1 mile). The connection lasts for a number of minutes equal to your Sorcerer level.

features.name: Psionic Sorcery (6th Level)
features.description: When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher from your Psionic Spells feature, you can cast it by spending a number of sorcery points equal to the spell's level instead of expending a spell slot. If you do so, the spell requires no verbal, somatic, or material components (unless the material components are consumed by the spell).

features.name: Psychic Defenses (6th Level)
features.description: You gain resistance to psychic damage and have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

features.name: Revelation in Flesh (14th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can spend 1 or more sorcery points to magically transform your body for 10 minutes. For each sorcery point spent, you gain one benefit: see invisible creatures, gain a flying speed, gain a swimming speed and water breathing, or become slimy and able to squeeze through 1-inch spaces.

features.name: Warping Implosion (18th Level)
features.description: As an action, you can teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 120 feet. Each creature within 30 feet of the space you left must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, it takes 3d10 force damage and is pulled toward your former space. On a success, it takes half damage and is not pulled.

name: Clockwork Soul
flavor_text: "The cosmic force of order has suffused your soul with a mechanik mutation. Your magic is a manifestation of the cosmic forces of order and law, perhaps stemming from a connection to Mechanus, the Clockwork Nirvana of Nirvana."
description: A sorcerer of absolute order. You gain an expanded spell list of abjuration and transmutation magic, can negate advantage and disadvantage, create wards of order to reduce damage, enter a trance that makes your rolls reliable, and eventually summon a cavalcade of modrons to restore order.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Clockwork Magic (1st Level)
features.description: You learn additional spells from the Sorcerer spell list, which must be abjuration or transmutation spells. These spells don't count against your number of spells known.

features.name: Restore Balance (1st Level)
features.description: When a creature within 60 feet of you is about to roll a d20 with advantage or disadvantage, you can use your reaction to prevent the roll from having advantage or disadvantage.

features.name: Bastion of Law (6th Level)
features.description: As an action, you can spend 1 to 5 sorcery points to create a magical ward around yourself or an ally within 30 feet. The ward has a number of d8s equal to the sorcery points spent. When the warded creature takes damage, it can spend one or more of the d8s, reducing the damage by the total rolled. The ward lasts until you finish a long rest or until you use this feature again.

features.name: Trance of Order (14th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can enter a trance of order for 1 minute. During this time, attack rolls against you can't benefit from advantage, and whenever you make an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can treat a roll of 9 or lower on the d20 as a 10.

features.name: Clockwork Cavalcade (18th Level)
features.description: As an action, you summon spirits of order in a 30-foot cube. You and creatures of your choice in the cube regain up to 100 hit points total (divided as you choose), and any objects or structures in the area are repaired. Additionally, spells and magical effects of 6th level or lower on creatures and objects in the area end.

name: Lunar Sorcery
flavor_text: "The moon is almost synonymous with magic itself. Countless cultures have revered its power over the tides, its influence on our mood, and the safety its light provides. As a Lunar Sorcery sorcerer, you can embody and channel the powers of this mysterious celestial body."
description: A versatile sorcerer whose magic shifts with the phases of the moon. Each day you choose a lunar phase—Full Moon, New Moon, or Crescent Moon—which grants you a free 1st-level spell and determines bonus spells, metamagic cost reductions, and other benefits. You can change your phase as a bonus action, making you highly adaptable.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Lunar Embodiment (1st Level)
features.description: When you finish a long rest, choose a lunar phase: Full Moon, New Moon, or Crescent Moon. You learn additional spells associated with that phase (they don't count against your spells known), and you can cast the phase's 1st-level spell once without expending a spell slot.

features.name: Moon Fire (1st Level)
features.description: You learn the Sacred Flame cantrip. When you cast it, you can target two creatures within 5 feet of each other instead of one.

features.name: Lunar Boons (6th Level)
features.description: Each lunar phase is associated with two schools of magic (Full Moon: Abjuration/Divination; New Moon: Enchantment/Necromancy; Crescent Moon: Illusion/Transmutation). When you use Metamagic on a spell of a school associated with your current phase, you can reduce the sorcery point cost by 1. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

features.name: Waxing and Waning (6th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can spend 1 sorcery point to change your lunar phase to a different one.

features.name: Lunar Empowerment (14th Level)
features.description: You gain passive benefits based on your current phase:

features.name: Full Moon
features.description: You and allies within your light have advantage on Investigation and Perception checks.

features.name: New Moon
features.description: You have advantage on Stealth checks, and attacks against you have disadvantage while you are in darkness.

features.name: Crescent Moon
features.description: You gain resistance to necrotic and radiant damage.

features.name: Lunar Phenomenon (18th Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you can unleash the full power of your current phase.

features.name: Full Moon
features.description: Enemies within 30 feet must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be blinded until the end of their next turn, and one ally you can see regains hit points.

features.name: New Moon
features.description: Enemies within 30 feet take necrotic damage and have their speed reduced, while you become invisible.

features.name: Crescent Moon
features.description: You and one willing creature within 30 feet teleport to unoccupied spaces you can see and gain resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn. Each phase's Lunar Phenomenon can be used once per long rest, or again by spending 5 sorcery points.

name: The Archfey
flavor_text: Your patron is a lord or lady of the fey, a creature of legend who holds secrets forgotten before the mortal races were born. This entity is often inscrutable and whimsical, and might be a figure like the Prince of Frost, the Queen of Air and Darkness, Titania of the Summer Court, or an ancient hag. You might have a single pact with one archfey or weave a web of favors and debts with a spectrum of fey beings.
description: A Warlock whose pact grants them the beguiling and terrifying power of the Feywild. You gain abilities to charm or frighten foes, teleport short distances, and turn attacks against you back on your attacker. The archetype excels at battlefield control, evasion, and social manipulation.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (1st Level)
features.description: You can choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell, adding faerie fire and sleep (1st), calm emotions and phantasmal force (2nd), blink and plant growth (3rd), dominate beast and greater invisibility (4th), and dominate person and seeming (5th) to your warlock spell list.

features.name: Fey Presence (1st Level)
features.description: As an action, you can cause each creature in a 10-foot cube originating from you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. Creatures that fail are either charmed or frightened by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn. You must finish a short or long rest before using this feature again.

features.name: Misty Escape (6th Level)
features.description: When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You remain invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or cast a spell. You must finish a short or long rest before using this feature again.

features.name: Beguiling Defenses (10th Level)
features.description: You are immune to being charmed. In addition, when another creature attempts to charm you, you can use your reaction to attempt to turn the charm back on that creature, forcing it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

features.name: Dark Delirium (14th Level)
features.description: As an action, you can plunge a creature within 60 feet into an illusory realm. It must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it is charmed or frightened (your choice) for 1 minute, or until your concentration is broken. While charmed or frightened in this way, the creature is blinded and deafened to its actual surroundings. You must finish a short or long rest before using this feature again.

name: The Fiend
flavor_text: You have made a pact with a fiend from the lower planes of existence, a being whose aims are evil, even if you strive against those aims. Such beings desire the corruption or destruction of all things, ultimately including you. Powerful fiends include demon lords like Demogorgon and Orcus, archdevils like Asmodeus and Mephistopheles, and mighty pit fiends and balors.
description: A Warlock who draws power from the Lower Planes, gaining resilience and the ability to hurl foes through hell itself. This patron grants you temporary vitality when you slay enemies, the ability to bend luck, and resistance to a chosen damage type.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (1st Level)
features.description: Your patron adds spells like burning hands, command, blindness/deafness, scorching ray, fireball, stinking cloud, fire shield, wall of fire, flame strike, and hallow to your warlock spell list. Dark One’s Blessing (1st Level): When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum of 1). Dark One’s Own Luck (6th Level): When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any effects occur. You must finish a short or long rest before using this feature again.

features.name: Fiendish Resilience (10th Level)
features.description: When you finish a short or long rest, you can choose one damage type (except force). You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature. Damage from magical weapons or silvered weapons ignores this resistance.

features.name: Hurl Through Hell (14th Level)
features.description: When you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to instantly transport the target through the Lower Planes. The creature disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape. At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it previously occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space. If the target is not a fiend, it takes 10d10 psychic damage as it reels from its horrific experience. You must finish a long rest before using this feature again.

name: The Great Old One
flavor_text: Your patron is a mysterious entity whose nature is utterly foreign to the fabric of reality. It might be an elder god like Tharizdun, the Chained God; Zargon, the Returner; Hadar, the Dark Hunger; or Great Cthulhu himself. The motives of these beings are incomprehensible, and the Great Old One might be indifferent to your existence. But the secrets you've learned allow you to draw strange magic from it.
description: A Warlock who has unearthed forbidden lore of ineffable beings, gaining psionic-like abilities. You can create telepathic links, ward yourself with alien magic, and even create a thrall from a slain humanoid.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (1st Level)
features.description: Your patron adds spells like dissonant whispers, Tasha's hideous laughter, detect thoughts, phantasmal force, clairvoyance, hunger of Hadar, confusion, summon aberration, telekinesis, and modify memory to your warlock spell list.

features.name: Awakened Mind (1st Level)
features.description: You can form a telepathic connection between your mind and the mind of another. As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet. You and the chosen creature can communicate telepathically with each other while you are within a number of miles equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1 mile). The connection lasts for a number of minutes equal to your warlock level.

features.name: Entropic Ward (6th Level)
features.description: When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on that roll. If the attack misses you, your next attack roll against the creature has advantage if you make it before the end of your next turn. You must finish a short or long rest before using this feature again.

features.name: Thought Shield (10th Level)
features.description: Your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it. You also have resistance to psychic damage, and whenever a creature deals psychic damage to you, that creature takes the same amount of damage.

features.name: Create Thrall (14th Level)
features.description: You gain the ability to infect a humanoid's mind with the alien magic of your patron. You can use your action to touch an incapacitated humanoid, which then becomes charmed by you until a remove curse spell is cast on it, the charmed condition is removed from it, or you use this feature again. You can communicate telepathically with the charmed creature as long as the two of you are on the same plane of existence.

name: The Undying
flavor_text: Death holds no sway over your patron, who has unlocked the secrets of everlasting life. This entity could be a lich, a mummy lord, or a vampire, and it has imparted a fraction of its power to you. Your pact allows you to defy death, sustain yourself without food or water, and even reattach severed limbs.
description: A Warlock whose patron has conquered death, granting you unnatural resilience. You can ward off undead, regain hit points when you cheat death, and eventually sustain yourself indefinitely without mortal needs.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (1st Level)
features.description: Your patron adds spells like false life, ray of sickness, blindness/deafness, silence, feign death, speak with dead, aura of life, death ward, and contagion to your warlock spell list.

features.name: Among the Dead (1st Level)
features.description: You learn the spare the dying cantrip, which counts as a warlock cantrip for you. You have advantage on saving throws against disease. Additionally, undead have difficulty harming you: if an undead targets you directly with an attack or harmful spell, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be forced to choose a new target.

features.name: Defy Death (6th Level)
features.description: You can regain hit points equal to 1d8 + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 hit point) when you succeed on a death saving throw or when you stabilize a creature with spare the dying. You must finish a long rest before using this feature again.

features.name: Undying Nature (10th Level)
features.description: You can hold your breath indefinitely, and you don't require food, water, or sleep, although you still require rest to reduce exhaustion. You also age at a slower rate: for every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year, and you are immune to being magically aged.

features.name: Indestructible Life (14th Level)
features.description: On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d8 + your warlock level. Additionally, if you put a severed body part of yours back in place when you use this feature, the part reattaches. You must finish a short or long rest before using this feature again.

name: The Celestial
flavor_text: Your patron is a powerful being of the Upper Planes. You have bound yourself to an ancient empyrean, a couatl, a sphinx, a unicorn, or another heavenly entity. Your pact allows you to experience a hint of the holy light that illuminates the multiverse and to channel it to heal wounds and sear foes.
description: A Warlock who draws power from the heavens, gaining access to radiant and healing magic. You can heal with a pool of celestial energy, resist radiant damage, and eventually sear your enemies with holy fire.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (1st Level)
features.description: Your patron adds spells like cure wounds, guiding bolt, flaming sphere, lesser restoration, daylight, revivify, guardian of faith, wall of fire, greater restoration, and flame strike to your warlock spell list.

features.name: Bonus Cantrips (1st Level)
features.description: You learn the light and sacred flame cantrips, which count as warlock cantrips for you.

features.name: Healing Light (1st Level)
features.description: You gain a pool of d6s equal to 1 + your warlock level. As a bonus action, you can heal one creature you can see within 60 feet, expending dice from the pool. The maximum number of dice you can expend at once equals your Charisma modifier (minimum of one die).

features.name: Radiant Soul (6th Level)
features.description: You gain resistance to radiant damage. Once per turn when you cast a spell that deals radiant or fire damage, you can add your Charisma modifier to that spell's damage against one of its targets.

features.name: Celestial Resilience (10th Level)
features.description: You gain temporary hit points whenever you finish a short or long rest. These temporary hit points equal your warlock level + your Charisma modifier.

features.name: Searing Vengeance (14th Level)
features.description: When you or an ally within 30 feet is reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to release a burst of radiant energy. The creature regains hit points equal to half its hit point maximum and can stand up if it wishes. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet takes radiant damage equal to 2d8 + your Charisma modifier and is blinded until the end of its next turn. You must finish a long rest before using this feature again.

name: The Hexblade
flavor_text: You have made your pact with a mysterious entity from the Shadowfell—a force that manifests in sentient magic weapons carved from the stuff of shadow. The mighty sword Blackrazor is the most notable of these weapons, which have been spread across the multiverse over the ages. The shadowy force behind these weapons can offer power to warlocks who form pacts with it.
description: A Warlock who blends martial prowess with shadow magic, cursing foes and wielding a powerful sentient weapon. You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons, allowing you to thrive in melee combat.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (1st Level)
features.description: Your patron adds spells like shield, wrathful smite, blur, branding smite, blink, elemental weapon, phantasmal killer, staggering smite, banishing smite, and cone of cold to your warlock spell list. Hexblade’s Curse (1st Level): As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet. The target is cursed for 1 minute. Until the curse ends, you gain a bonus to damage rolls against the target equal to your proficiency bonus, any attack roll you make against it is a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20, and if it dies, you regain hit points equal to your warlock level + your Charisma modifier. You must finish a short or long rest before using this feature again.

features.name: Hex Warrior (1st Level)
features.description: You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons. When you finish a long rest, you can touch one weapon (lacking the two-handed property) and use your Charisma modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls. This benefit extends to pact weapons if you have the Pact of the Blade feature.

features.name: Accursed Specter (6th Level)
features.description: When you slay a humanoid, you can cause its spirit to rise as a specter, which gains temporary hit points equal to half your warlock level and obeys your verbal commands. It remains in your service until the end of your next long rest. You must finish a long rest before using this feature again.

features.name: Armor of Hexes (10th Level)
features.description: If the target of your Hexblade’s Curse hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to roll a d6. On a 4 or higher, the attack instead misses you, regardless of its roll.

features.name: Master of Hexes (14th Level)
features.description: You can spread your Hexblade’s Curse from a slain creature to a new target. When a creature cursed by you dies, you can apply the curse to a different creature you can see within 30 feet, without expending a use of the feature.

name: The Fathomless
flavor_text: You have plunged into a pact with the deeps. An entity of the ocean, the Elemental Plane of Water, or another otherworldly sea now allows you to draw on its thalassic power. This patron might be a godly dragon turtle, a tentacled monstrosity venerated by kuo-toa cultists, or a primordial spirit of the deep ocean.
description: A Warlock who commands the power of the sea, summoning spectral tentacles to strike and slow foes, gaining a swimming speed, and eventually teleporting through bodies of water.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (1st Level)
features.description: Your patron adds spells like create or destroy water, thunderwave, gust of wind, silence, lightning bolt, sleet storm, control water, summon elemental (water only), Bigby's hand (as a tentacle), and cone of cold to your warlock spell list.

features.name: Tentacle of the Deeps (1st Level)
features.description: You can magically summon a spectral tentacle that strikes at your foes. As a bonus action, you can create a 10-foot-long tentacle at a point you can see within 60 feet. The tentacle lasts for 1 minute. When you create it and as a bonus action on subsequent turns, you can direct it to attack a creature within 10 feet of it, dealing cold or lightning damage (your choice) equal to 1d8 + your Charisma modifier, and reducing its speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Gift of the Sea (1st Level)
features.description: You gain a swimming speed of 40 feet, and you can breathe underwater.

features.name: Oceanic Soul (6th Level)
features.description: You gain resistance to cold damage. Additionally, when you are fully immersed in water, you can telepathically communicate with any creature that has a swimming speed and is also fully immersed in water within 120 feet of you.

features.name: Guardian Coil (6th Level)
features.description: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll against you or an ally, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by 1d8 + your warlock level. If the damage is reduced to 0, the attacker takes cold or lightning damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

features.name: Grasping Tentacles (10th Level)
features.description: You learn the Evard's black tentacles spell. It doesn't count against your number of warlock spells known, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Fathomless Plunge (14th Level)
features.description: You can magically open temporary conduits to watery destinations. As an action, you can teleport yourself and up to five other willing creatures within 30 feet of you to any body of water you have seen within 1 mile. You all arrive in the nearest unoccupied space within 30 feet of the destination.

name: The Genie
flavor_text: You have made a pact with one of the rarest and most powerful types of genies, a being of the Elemental Planes. This patron is a noble among its kind, such as a dao, a djinni, an efreeti, or a marid. Your pact grants you mastery over the elements and the ability to grant minor wishes.
description: A Warlock whose patron is a noble genie, granting you an elemental affinity, a magical vessel to retreat into, and the ability to grant limited wishes to others. You gain resistance to a damage type based on your patron and can eventually summon a member of its court.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (1st Level)
features.description: Your patron adds spells based on its element (e.g., burning hands and scorching ray for an efreeti; thunderwave and gust of wind for a djinni) to your warlock spell list. Genie’s Vessel (1st Level): You gain a magical vessel (a Tiny object) that you can use as a spellcasting focus. You can use an action to disappear into the vessel for up to 4 hours (or until you use a bonus action to leave). While inside, you are aware of your surroundings, can hear and see outside, and can't be targeted by attacks or spells. You can also use the vessel to store items. You can use this feature once per long rest.

features.name: Elemental Gift (1st Level)
features.description: You gain a resistance to a damage type based on your patron: bludgeoning (dao), thunder (djinni), fire (efreeti), or cold (marid). You can also use a bonus action to gain a flying speed of 30 feet for 10 minutes, during which you can hover.

features.name: Sanctuary Vessel (6th Level)
features.description: When you enter your Genie's Vessel, you can choose up to five willing creatures to enter with you. While inside, they gain the benefits of a short rest, and you can add your proficiency bonus to any Hit Dice they spend.

features.name: Elemental Resistance (10th Level)
features.description: You gain resistance to a damage type of your choice from your patron's list. This is in addition to the resistance from your Elemental Gift.

features.name: Limited Wish (14th Level)
features.description: You can use an action to speak your patron's name and request a minor wish. The wish can replicate the effect of any spell of 6th level or lower that doesn't require material components. You must finish 1d4 long rests before using this feature again.

name: The Undead
class_name: Warlock (Source: Van Richten's Guide to Ravenloft)
flavor_text: You've made a pact with a deathless entity, a being that has cheated the grave and now bestrides the world as a lord of the dead. This patron might be a vampire, a lich, or another powerful undead being. Your pact allows you to take on a terrifying form, drain the life from your foes, and eventually project your spirit from your body.
description: A Warlock who draws power from a deathless patron, granting you a fearsome Form of Dread, the ability to replace damage with necrotic energy, and a spirit that can leave your body behind. You are a master of fear and decay.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (1st Level)
features.description: Your patron adds spells like bane, false life, blindness/deafness, phantasmal force, and speak with dead to your warlock spell list.

features.name: Form of Dread (1st Level)
features.description: As a bonus action, you transform for 1 minute. You gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your warlock level, you can force a creature you hit with an attack to make a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn (once per turn), and you are immune to the frightened condition. You can transform a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.

features.name: Grave Touched (6th Level)
features.description: You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe. Once during each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack and roll damage, you can replace the damage type with necrotic damage. While using your Form of Dread, you roll one additional damage die when determining the necrotic damage.

features.name: Necrotic Husk (10th Level)
features.description: You have resistance to necrotic damage. While using your Form of Dread, you are instead immune to necrotic damage. When reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to drop to 1 hit point instead and cause your body to erupt with deathly energy, dealing necrotic damage equal to 2d10 + your warlock level to creatures of your choice within 30 feet. You then gain 1 level of exhaustion. You must finish 1d4 long rests before using this reaction again.

features.name: Spirit Projection (14th Level)
features.description: As an action, you can project your spirit from your body for up to 1 hour (or until your concentration is broken). Your body is unconscious and in suspended animation. Your spirit has your game statistics but not your possessions, and it can fly, hover, and move through creatures and objects as difficult terrain. You and your body share damage, and you gain other benefits while projecting, such as resistance to physical damage and the ability to cast conjuration and necromancy spells without verbal or somatic components.

name: School of Abjuration
flavor_text: The School of Abjuration emphasizes magic that blocks, banishes, or protects. Detractors of this school say that its tradition is about denial and negation, but you know better. You are a master of protection, using your magic to shield the weak and punish the aggressive.
description: The defensive wizard. Abjurers create powerful arcane wards that absorb damage, project those wards onto allies, and eventually gain advantage on saving throws against spells and resistance to spell damage. They are the ultimate protectors on the battlefield.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Abjuration Savant (2nd Level)
features.description: The gold and time you must spend to copy an abjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Arcane Ward (2nd Level)
features.description: When you cast an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher, you can create a magical ward on yourself. The ward has hit points equal to twice your wizard level + your Intelligence modifier. Whenever you take damage, the ward absorbs it instead. The ward's hit points are replenished when you cast another abjuration spell.

features.name: Projected Ward (6th Level)
features.description: When a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, you can use your reaction to have your Arcane Ward absorb that damage instead.

features.name: Improved Abjuration (10th Level)
features.description: When you cast an abjuration spell that requires you to make an ability check as part of the casting (like Counterspell or Dispel Magic), you add your proficiency bonus to that check.

features.name: Spell Resistance (14th Level)
features.description: You have advantage on saving throws against spells, and you have resistance against the damage of spells.

name: School of Conjuration
flavor_text: As a conjurer, you favor spells that produce objects and creatures out of thin air. You can conjure billowing clouds of killing fog or summon creatures from elsewhere to fight on your behalf.
description: The summoner and teleporter. Conjurers excel at creating objects and creatures, and they are masters of teleportation magic, able to swap places with allies and ensure their summoned creatures are exceptionally durable.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Conjuration Savant (2nd Level)
features.description: The gold and time you must spend to copy a conjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Minor Conjuration (2nd Level)
features.description: You can use your action to conjure a nonmagical inanimate object in your hand or on the ground in an unoccupied space that you can see within 10 feet. The object cannot be larger than 3 feet on a side and weigh more than 10 pounds, and its form must be that of a nonmagical object that you have seen.

features.name: Benign Transposition (6th Level)
features.description: As an action, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, or you can choose a willing Small or Medium creature within 30 feet and swap places with it.

features.name: Focused Conjuration (10th Level)
features.description: While you are concentrating on a conjuration spell, your concentration can't be broken as a result of taking damage.

features.name: Durable Summons (14th Level)
features.description: Any creature that you summon or create with a conjuration spell has 30 temporary hit points.

name: School of Divination
flavor_text: The counsel of a diviner is sought by royalty and commoners alike, for all seek a clearer understanding of the past, present, and future. As a diviner, you strive to part the veils of space, time, and consciousness so that you can see clearly.
description: The seer and fate-manipulator. Diviners gain fragments of the future that they can use to replace any attack roll, saving throw, or ability check, making them masters of control and foresight. They can also cast divination spells with remarkable efficiency.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Divination Savant (2nd Level)
features.description: The gold and time you must spend to copy a divination spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Portent (2nd Level)
features.description: When you finish a long rest, roll two d20s and record the numbers. You can replace any attack roll, saving throw, or ability check made by you or a creature that you can see with one of these foretelling rolls. You must choose to do so before the roll.

features.name: Expert Divination (6th Level)
features.description: When you cast a divination spell of 2nd level or higher using a spell slot, you regain one expended spell slot of a lower level.

features.name: The Third Eye (10th Level)
features.description: As an action, you can gain one of the following benefits: Darkvision (60 ft.), Ethereal Sight (see 60 ft. into the Ethereal Plane), Greater Comprehension (read any language), or See Invisibility.

features.name: Greater Portent (14th Level)
features.description: You roll three d20s for your Portent feature, rather than two.

name: School of Enchantment
flavor_text: As a member of the School of Enchantment, you have honed your ability to magically entrance and beguile other people and monsters. Some enchanters are peacemakers who bewitch the violent to lay down their arms and charm the cruel into showing mercy. Others are tyrants who magically bind the unwilling into their service.
description: The manipulator of minds. Enchanters can hypnotize foes with a gaze, turn an attacker's strike against them, and eventually alter a creature's memory to forget they were ever magically influenced.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Enchantment Savant (2nd Level)
features.description: The gold and time you must spend to copy an enchantment spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Hypnotic Gaze (2nd Level)
features.description: As an action, you can target one creature you can see within 5 feet. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you until the end of your next turn. While charmed, it is incapacitated and has a speed of 0.

features.name: Instinctive Charm (6th Level)
features.description: When a creature you can see within 30 feet makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to divert the attack, provided another creature is within the attack's range. The attacker must make a Wisdom saving throw or be forced to target the other creature instead.

features.name: Split Enchantment (10th Level)
features.description: When you cast an enchantment spell of 1st level or higher that targets only one creature, you can have it target a second creature.

features.name: Alter Memories (14th Level)
features.description: When you cast an enchantment spell to charm a creature, you can make the creature unaware that it was charmed. Additionally, you can use your action to try to make the creature forget some of the time it spent charmed.

name: School of Evocation
flavor_text: You focus your study on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast enemy armies from afar.
description: The blaster wizard. Evokers are the undisputed masters of raw damage, able to sculpt their spells to avoid harming allies, add their Intelligence modifier to damage rolls, and eventually deal maximum damage with their most powerful spells.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Evocation Savant (2nd Level)
features.description: The gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Sculpt Spells (2nd Level)
features.description: When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

features.name: Potent Cantrip (6th Level)
features.description: When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

features.name: Empowered Evocation (10th Level)
features.description: You can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.

features.name: Overchannel (14th Level)
features.description: When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell. The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it.

name: School of Illusion
flavor_text: You focus your studies on magic that dazzles the senses, befuddles the mind, and tricks even the wisest folk. Your magic is subtle, but the illusions crafted by your keen mind make the impossible seem real.
description: The master of deception. Illusionists can create minor illusions at will, reshape their existing illusions, and eventually make parts of their illusions real, blurring the line between fantasy and reality.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Illusion Savant (2nd Level)
features.description: The gold and time you must spend to copy an illusion spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Improved Minor Illusion (2nd Level)
features.description: You learn the Minor Illusion cantrip. If you already know it, you learn a different wizard cantrip of your choice. When you cast Minor Illusion, you can create both a sound and an image with a single casting.

features.name: Malleable Illusions (6th Level)
features.description: When you cast an illusion spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can use your action to change the nature of that illusion (using the spell's normal parameters for the illusion), provided that you can see the illusion.

features.name: Illusory Self (10th Level)
features.description: When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to interpose an illusory duplicate of yourself between you and the attacker, causing the attack to automatically miss you. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Illusory Reality (14th Level)
features.description: When you cast an illusion spell of 1st level or higher, you can choose one inanimate, nonmagical object that is part of the illusion and make that object real. The object remains real for 1 minute.

name: School of Necromancy
flavor_text: You focus your studies on the forces of life and death. You are a master of the macabre, using your magic to drain the life from your foes and to command the loyalty of the undead.
description: The commander of the dead. Necromancers steal life force from those they kill to heal themselves, raise armies of the undead, and eventually gain resistance to necrotic damage and the ability to command even powerful undead.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Necromancy Savant (2nd Level)
features.description: The gold and time you must spend to copy a necromancy spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Grim Harvest (2nd Level)
features.description: Once per turn when you kill one or more creatures with a spell of 1st level or higher, you regain hit points equal to twice the spell's level, or three times if it is a necromancy spell.

features.name: Undead Thralls (6th Level)
features.description: When you cast Animate Dead, you can target one additional corpse or pile of bones, creating another zombie or skeleton. Creatures you create with necromancy spells have their hit point maximum increased by your wizard level, and they add your proficiency bonus to their damage rolls.

features.name: Inured to Undeath (10th Level)
features.description: You have resistance to necrotic damage, and your hit point maximum can't be reduced.

features.name: Command Undead (14th Level)
features.description: You can use your action to try to command an undead creature you can see within 60 feet. It must make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. If it fails, it becomes friendly to you and obeys your commands for 1 hour or until you use this feature again.

name: School of Transmutation
flavor_text: You are a student of spells that modify energy and matter. To you, the world is not a fixed thing but a canvas on which you can paint your own reality. Your magic gives you the tools to become a smith of the very fabric of reality.
description: The alchemist and shapeshifter. Transmuters can magically transform one material into another, create a stone that grants them or an ally powerful benefits, and eventually use that stone to achieve effects like restoring life or granting a boost to physical attributes.
dm_guidelines: Not present in official source material.

features.name: Transmutation Savant (2nd Level)
features.description: The gold and time you must spend to copy a transmutation spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Minor Alchemy (2nd Level)
features.description: You can temporarily alter the physical properties of one nonmagical object, changing one material into another (e.g., wood into silver, stone into iron, copper into gold).

features.name: Transmuter's Stone (6th Level)
features.description: You can spend 8 hours creating a transmuter's stone that stores transmutation magic. You can benefit from the stone as long as you have it in your possession. You choose the stone's benefit (e.g., Darkvision, speed increase, proficiency in Constitution saves, resistance to a damage type).

features.name: Shapechanger (10th Level)
features.description: You can add the Polymorph spell to your spellbook, if it is not there already. You can cast Polymorph without expending a spell slot, but you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

features.name: Master Transmuter (14th Level)
features.description: You can use your action to consume the reserve of transmutation magic stored within your transmuter's stone in a single burst.
